items.content: As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world’s most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. He also wears a cool leather jacket.Which makes Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy — reportedly while her spying was known to US intelligence and even President Donald Trump — all the more shocking. The fallout goes well beyond his marriage, his reputation, or Nvidia itself. Experts tell The Verge the incident threatens to disrupt the entire US AI industry, potentially jeopardize national security, and could undermine America’s efforts to maintain its fragile technological lead over China in AI.“With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.”Nvidia is the undisputed leader in advanced computer chips, among the AI industry’s scarcest resources. While many ingredients go into building AI models — including talent, energy, capital, and data — top-tier chips are one of the most important, and Nvidia is one of a handful of companies with the expertise to design or manufacture them at the cutting edge. That makes it a gatekeeper to hardware that has become a key bottleneck in global AI development. US companies — including Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI — are racing to develop chips of their own, in part to reduce their dependence on Nvidia, even as they spend billions securing ever more compute.RelatedWhat could China get from Jensen Huang?The future of AI hinges on… Jensen Huang’s sex life?Here’s what Trump said he knew about Jensen HuangFor China, the US’s main rival at the frontier of AI, that bottleneck is even tighter. To maintain its technological lead, the US has restricted the sale of the most advanced AI chips to the country in the hopes of slowing its progress in the sector, which has been impressive and is thought to trail the US by a matter of months. In response, China has made developing domestic alternatives a strategic national priority, though its leaders still lag Nvidia at the bleeding edge. At the same time, a thriving black market for restricted Nvidia chips has emerged.Experts tell The Verge that China could exploit access to Nvidia to accelerate its own development, or to impede the US development of AI.Getting its hands on more Nvidia chips is the most obvious win for Beijing, says Emily Kilcrease, a senior fellow and director of the energy, economics, and security program at the Center for a New American Security (CNAS) think tank. China has advantages in other parts of the AI race — including abundant energy and a solid ecosystem of open weight models — but without the latest Nvidia chips, it “cannot close the gap with US frontier capabilities,” Kilcrease tells The Verge. “With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.”It is not clear how successful the alleged spying operation has been on that front. There is no public evidence indicating that Huang himself has helped direct restricted Nvidia chips toward China or that sensitive information about them was obtained from him. But companies linked to the alleged spy, Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen — have reportedly enabled at least $7 billion of Nvidia chip sales to China.Brookings fellow Kyle Chan tells The Verge that a concern for US industry could be that companies with alleged ties to China may have had priority access to Nvidia’s latest GPUs. “In a time of chip scarcity,” that would make it much harder for American companies to access them, Chan says.Huang is also a prominent critic of American restrictions on chip sales, and Nvidia spends a formidable amount lobbying in Washington. Last year, he successfully secured White House approval to start exporting Nvidia’s H200 AI GPU chips to “approved customers” in China and other countries. Crucially, Huang also has the ear of President Trump as well as other world leaders, giving him great influence over policy decisions.Hardware is not the only thing of value China could get from close access to Huang, Sunny Cheung, a fellow for China studies at the Jamestown Foundation think tank, tells The Verge. “I actually think too many people are focused on whether somebody managed to steal Nvidia’s trade secrets,” Cheung says, calling it a “very narrow way” of looking at espionage. “I would hope Jensen Huang isn’t foolish enough to hand over the blueprints for Nvidia’s next-generation chips to a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.”The Nvidia CEO’s relationships with other tech executives, senior policymakers, and Trump himself give him an unusually intimate view into how some of the most powerful people in the US are thinking and planning. Beijing could use information on how American companies are planning major infrastructure expansions, their compute requirements, or broad industry trends to inform its own investments and industrial strategy, Cheung says.Huang’s intelligence value could extend well beyond AI, too. “That information alone could be extremely valuable,” says Cheung, pointing to insights Beijing could glean into White House thinking about export controls or the private views of Silicon Valley executives on China and Taiwan.“When so much of America’s AI infrastructure depends on one company, any significant security or governance problem at Nvidia can create uncertainty across the industry.”But helping China advance is only one side of this equation. Disrupting Nvidia — as this scandal clearly has — could destabilize America’s entire AI industry. More than most companies, Nvidia is remarkably closely tied to the identity and reputation of its rockstar CEO. Huang cofounded the company more than three decades ago, and ever since then he has served as its president, chief executive, and a member of the board of directors. Despite holding a relatively small stake in the company, in many ways Nvidia is Jensen Huang. Nvidia shares have slumped since news of the affair broke.“When so much of America’s AI infrastructure depends on one company, any significant security or governance problem at Nvidia can create uncertainty across the industry,” Cheung says.Kilcrease echoes those concerns, warning that the scandal could “destabilize” the company. At the very least, she says the various investigations already underway “will consume an immense amount of bandwidth within the company,” creating a very real risk of weighing down Nvidia’s day-to-day operations. If those distractions begin to affect Nvidia’s ability to execute — slowing decisions, product rollouts, or the allocation of already scarce chips — the consequences could quickly reach customers. The AI labs and hyperscalers such as OpenAI and Anthropic “could have a real issue accessing the vast amounts of compute they need,” Kilcrease says, adding that switching to other hardware “takes time.”In a race to build increasingly powerful AI, time is a precious resource. Experts say China trails the US closely, meaning that even modest delays for American companies can help Chinese rivals catch up. Nvidia is almost certain to face further disruption as investigations continue, though the extent to which the turmoil will roil the rest of the industry may be difficult to measure.For China, however, the scandal could be about to backfire spectacularly now everything is out in the open. “The odds of AI chip control legislation being passed in Congress just went through the roof,” Kilcrease says.Correction, Tuesday November 10th: A sentence in this article misstated that Anthropic is the leader in advanced computer chips. It is Nvidia.

items.titleZh: 美国正在赢得人工智能竞赛，黄仁勋本可能搞砸它
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达CEO黄仁勋承认与一名疑似中国间谍的女性有婚外情，据报道这段关系发生在美国情报界甚至特朗普已知晓其间谍嫌疑之时。事件影响远超个人婚姻、声誉或英伟达本身。专家警告，这可能扰乱美国整个人工智能产业、危及国家安全，并削弱美国在AI领域对中国的脆弱技术领先优势。

背景上，英伟达是全球先进AI芯片无可争议的领导者。构建AI模型需要人才、能源、资本和数据，但顶级芯片是最关键资源之一；英伟达是少数能够设计或制造前沿芯片的公司，因而成为全球AI开发关键硬件瓶颈的“守门人”。Meta、Anthropic、OpenAI等美国公司一边投入数十亿美元锁定算力，一边竞相自研芯片以减少对英伟达的依赖。对中国而言，这一瓶颈更紧：美国限制最先进AI芯片对华销售，以减缓中国进展；中国被认为在AI前沿仅落后美国数月，已把国产替代列为国家战略优先，但最前沿仍落后英伟达，同时受限英伟达芯片的黑市活跃。

专家指出，中国若获得更多英伟达芯片，最直接收益是加速自身AI发展。新美国安全中心专家艾米丽·基尔克雷斯表示，中国在能源和开放权重模型生态等方面有优势，但若没有最新英伟达芯片，“无法缩小与美国前沿能力的差距”；有了这些芯片，美国领先优势“可能在数周或数月内消失”。目前没有公开证据表明黄仁勋本人帮助将受限芯片导向中国或泄露敏感信息，但与疑似间谍爱丽丝·黄（与黄仁勋无亲属关系）有关联的公司据报促成了至少70亿美元的英伟达芯片对华销售。布鲁金斯学会专家陈凯尔认为，疑似与中国有关联的公司可能优先获得英伟达最新GPU，在芯片稀缺时期会加大美国企业获取难度。

黄仁勋还是美国芯片销售限制的知名批评者，英伟达在华盛顿投入大量游说。去年他成功争取白宫批准向中国等国“批准客户”出口H200 AI GPU。他同时与特朗普及其他国家领导人关系密切，对政策有较大影响力。詹姆斯敦基金会专家张颂恩认为，外界过度关注是否窃取英伟达商业秘密是“非常狭窄”的视角；黄仁勋与科技高管、高级政策制定者和特朗普的密切关系，使其能洞察美国最有权势人物的想法和计划。北京可利用美国公司基础设施扩张计划、算力需求、行业趋势、白宫出口管制思路以及硅谷高管对华对台私下看法等信息，服务自身投资和产业战略，这些情报价值可能远超AI领域。

另一方面，丑闻对英伟达的扰乱可能波及整个美国AI产业。英伟达与黄仁勋个人身份高度绑定：他三十多年前联合创办公司，长期担任总裁、CEO和董事，尽管持股相对较少，但英伟达在不少方面就是黄仁勋。丑闻曝光后英伟达股价下跌。张颂恩称，当美国AI基础设施如此依赖一家公司时，英伟达任何重大安全或治理问题都会给全行业带来不确定性。基尔克雷斯警告，调查将消耗公司大量精力，若分散注意力影响决策、产品推出或稀缺芯片分配，OpenAI、Anthropic等AI实验室和超大规模云厂商可能难以获得所需海量算力，而切换其他硬件需要时间。在AI竞赛中时间宝贵，美国公司哪怕 modest 延迟，也可能帮助中国对手追赶。

不过，事件全面公开后也可能反噬中国。基尔克雷斯认为，美国国会通过AI芯片出口管制立法的概率“刚刚大幅上升”。总体看，这一丑闻的核心风险不只是可能的芯片或技术泄露，而是英伟达治理与声誉受冲击后，对美国AI算力供应、政策走向和中美技术竞争态势产生的连锁不确定性。

items.title: Microsoft lobbies against potential ban on Chinese optical networking gear for AI data centers as FCC mulls restricting imports
items.description: The ITI is lobbying against the ban of these optical transceivers needed by data centers to convert electrical signals into optical signals.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Microsoft, the tech giant that is building 35 data centers around the U.S. and has plans for 134 more, has reportedly met with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and the National Security Council as the FCC is considering an import ban on Chinese optical transceivers. According to Reuters, the company, alongside the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI), is lobbying against the move.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible“It really threatens to arguably grind (the data center rollout) to a halt,” ITI Executive Vice President of Policy and General Counsel John Miller said. He also added, “Those chips, without optical transceivers, literally could just sit there waiting around unutilized until you actually have the transceivers to essentially connect them together,” referring to the AI chips that data centers use.Optical transceivers are tiny modules plugged into hardware that convert their electrical signals into light signals, allowing data to be transmitted as light pulses across fiber optics. Data centers increasingly use optical transceivers and fiber optics to transmit data between AI GPUs and server racks, as they’re faster, offer lower latency, require less power, and generate less heat compared to traditional copper connections. However, Chinese companies currently supply 66% of the global market, meaning banning them from supplying data centers in the U.S. would more than halve the available supply, thereby exacerbating the various shortages that have been pummeling the industry.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: However, there are concerns that some of these transceivers could be compromised by Beijing and be used to steal data, install malware, or remotely disrupt American data centers, which is why the FCC is considering the restriction, just like how it banned Huawei from the U.S. telecommunications network. But unlike Huawei, which had many established competitors in the telecommunications hardware industry, only two U.S.-based companies produce optical transceivers that data centers need — Coherent and Lumentum. While these firms could produce optical transceivers to compete with Chinese offerings, they simply do not have the scale to make up for the shortfall if the FCC bans Chinese imports today.One compromise floated by the Trump administration is that it would only ban Chinese optical transceivers capable of hitting 3.2 terabits per second. While this technology already exists, its production isn’t expected to expand until 2028, with installation not beginning until 2029. This should give American producers time to ramp up their own output, although the suggestion is still under consideration. items.titleZh: 微软游说反对可能禁止中国光网络设备用于AI数据中心，FCC正考虑限制进口
items.descriptionZh:
美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）正在考虑对中国产光模块（光收发器）实施进口禁令，这一潜在举措已引发微软等科技公司和行业组织的密集游说。据报道，微软已与白宫科学和技术政策办公室及国家安全委员会会面，并与信息技术产业委员会（ITI）共同反对该禁令。背景是微软正在美国建设35个数据中心，并计划再建134个，而光模块是这些AI数据中心实现高速互联的关键部件。ITI政策执行副总裁兼总法律顾问约翰·米勒警告，禁令“可能使数据中心部署事实上陷入停滞”；没有光模块，AI芯片即使安装到位也只能闲置，无法相互连接和投入计算。

从技术原理看，光模块是插入服务器、交换机等硬件的小型模块，负责把电信号转换为光信号，使数据能以光脉冲形式通过光纤传输。随着AI集群规模扩大，数据中心越来越多地在AI GPU与服务器机架之间使用光模块和光纤连接，因为相比传统铜缆，光连接速度更快、延迟更低、功耗更小、发热更少。当前中国厂商供应全球约66%的光模块市场，若美国禁止其产品进入本国数据中心，可用供应将减少一半以上，进一步加剧该行业已面临的短缺。

安全担忧是FCC考虑限制的主要原因：部分美国方面担心中国产光模块可能被北京利用，用于窃取数据、植入恶意软件或远程破坏美国数据中心。这一逻辑与此前FCC以国家安全为由禁止华为设备进入美国电信网络类似。但不同于华为所在电信硬件行业有较多成熟替代厂商，美国本土目前只有Coherent和Lumentum两家公司生产数据中心所需的光模块；即便它们能够扩产并与中国产品竞争，其规模也不足以在禁令立即生效的情况下填补供应缺口。

为缓解矛盾，特朗普政府内部曾讨论一项折中方案：只禁止能够达到3.2太比特/秒（Tbps）速率中国光模块。该技术已经存在，但预计到2028年才会扩大生产，2029年才开始安装，这理论上可为美国生产商争取扩产时间。不过，该建议仍在考虑之中。总体来看，禁令若实施，将同时冲击美国AI数据中心建设进度、供应链稳定和国家安全政策，而替代产能与时间表仍是关键变量。

items.title: AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’
items.description: Nvidia and Arm have new “agentic CPUs,” a title that high-ranking AMD employees are pushing back against with the launch of Zen 6 EPYC Venice CPUs.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 11 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Two prominent voices within AMD agree that the company didn’t design its new Zen 6 family, codenamed Venice, explicitly for agentic AI in a clear shot at Nvidia and Arm, who’ve both described their latest data center CPUs as “agentic” in nature. In separate talks, AMD’s chief Zen architect Mike Clark and corporate VP Madhu Rangarajan said that the company didn’t predict the agentic wave when Zen 6 development started.Go deeper with TH Premium: CPU (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Intel VP Robert Hallock sets Nova Lake expectations, teases return to Raptor Lake for DDR4 platformsCPU scaling with DLSSIntel's one-two punch plan in desktop CPUs is taking shapeBenchmarking AMD's BC-250, offering Steam Machine-like performance at half the priceAMD splits Zen 7 into three EPYC families for 2028 and starts selling server CPUs by the agent We just wrapped up testing AMD's Venice CPUs, which you can read more about in our Zen 6 benchmarking article.CPU development cycles are measured in years, and given that the agentic frenzy around CPUs hit around March of this year, it’s unreasonable to expect that anyone has developed silicon specifically for agentic AI, much less a general-purpose data center CPU. And still, Nvidia claims its Vera CPU was “purpose-built” for agentic AI, while Arm says its AGI CPU was “designed for the demands of agentic AI.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: “We think that the EPYC 9006 CPU is the best CPU for the agentic era, and spoiler alert, we didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing and purpose-built something for agentic,” said Rangarajan in a session with media. “The reality is an agentic workflow is a diverse set of tasks… and in order to execute those tasks well, you need compute that is able to handle a diverse set of workloads with a full portfolio.”Introducing the Zen 6 microarchitecture, Mike Clark agreed with the sentiment: “I’m not going to mislead and act like I knew agentic computing was coming, or we knew it, but we did strongly believe that the CPU would always have a place in the software ecosystem of AI… And as agentic [has] blown up, we [are] able to now deploy that for agentic compute workloads.” You may like Modal taps Nvidia Vera CPUs after firm's internal tests show 2x throughput over Intel and AMD chips OpenAI’s Jalapeño ASICs are deployed alongside AMD EPYC ‘Turin’ CPUs as hosts, not Nvidia's Vera Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests As AMD rolls out its next-generation microarchitecture with Venice CPUs, it’s targeting the messaging from Arm and Nvidia, which have posed the most direct threat to AMD’s continued rise in the data center on the back of agentic workloads. And indeed, there are performance vectors where Nvidia’s Vera looks strong for agentic workloads, as you can see in our Nvidia Vera testing. AMD’s argument, however, is that agentic AI calls for a broad range of CPUs just as general-purpose workloads do, pushing back on the single-SKU approach of Nvidia and Arm.Our testing of two AMD Venice chips supports that argument, as well, with the dense EPYC 9996 with its 256 cores and 512 threads offering peak throughput performance, while the frequency-optimized EPYC 9686F goes toe-to-toe with Vera in the role of an AI host node. AMD is launching two additional ranges next year, with Venice-X targeting HPC with its 3D-stack cache, and Verano going directly after Vera as an AI host node with an LPDDR5X memory system.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsAlthough the workload characteristics of agentic AI are still in the process of being defined, we have a better understanding of how those loops work now than we did at the beginning of the year. And like all complex topics, the answer to what is important in a CPU for agentic AI is the always-disappointing “it depends.”As we break down in our early testing procedure for agentic AI, the workload characteristics and demand on the CPU/memory are defined by what the agent is doing, and in the data center, what several agents are doing at high concurrency when sandboxed. A coding agent will generally call more tools that are taxing on the CPU than a web browsing agent, for example, while an agent that queries a database may call for strong memory performance.Of course, there are some vectors of performance that can’t be addressed with different SKUs (such as that strong memory performance). However, the potential diversity of agentic workloads certainly makes an argument for CPU variety. At a most basic level, an agentic loop allows the LLM to understand functions you’ve defined, and then pass arguments to those functions to execute them. We’re talking about a workload as broad as what you can define in a function in languages like Python and Rust. items.titleZh: AMD副总裁兼Zen首席架构师驳斥英伟达和Arm为智能体AI打造CPU的说法——“四年前我们不可能神奇地预知智能体会成为一种趋势”
items.descriptionZh:
AMD 两位核心高管——Zen 架构首席架构师 Mike Clark 和公司副总裁 Madhu Rangarajan——分别表示，AMD 新一代 Zen 6 家族（代号 Venice，对应 EPYC 9006 系列）并不是专门为“代理式 AI”（agentic AI）设计的。这与 Nvidia 和 Arm 的宣传形成直接对比：Nvidia 称其 Vera CPU 是“为代理式 AI 专门打造”，Arm 也称其 AGI CPU“为代理式 AI 的需求而设计”。AMD 高管坦言，Zen 6 的开发始于约四年前，当时公司并未预测到代理式 AI 浪潮，因此不可能“神奇地”提前专门设计芯片。但他们强调，CPU 在 AI 软件生态中始终有位置，而代理式 AI 的兴起正好让通用 CPU 能够部署到此类计算负载中。

文章的核心背景是，数据中心 CPU 厂商正围绕“agentic AI”展开营销竞争。Nvidia 和 Arm 试图用“专为代理式 AI 设计”来突出其新品，而 AMD 则反驳称，代理式 AI 工作流包含多样化任务，需要能够处理广泛负载的完整产品组合，而不是 Nvidia 和 Arm 所主张的单一 SKU 路线。Rangarajan 表示，EPYC 9006 是“代理式时代的最佳 CPU”，但这不是因为四年前预知了代理式 AI，而是因为代理式工作流本身需要多样化的计算能力。

从技术原理看，代理式 AI 的基本循环是：LLM 理解用户或系统定义的函数，然后向这些函数传递参数并执行。由此产生的负载范围非常广，几乎等同于 Python、Rust 等语言中可定义的函数范围。不同代理对 CPU 和内存的需求差异明显：例如编码代理通常会调用更多工具，对 CPU 压力更大；网页浏览代理的 CPU 负载相对较低；查询数据库的代理则可能需要更强的内存性能。在高并发数据中心环境中，多个代理在沙箱中同时运行，还会进一步放大对 CPU 和内存子系统的压力。因此，AMD 认为不存在一种单一 CPU 能完美覆盖所有代理式 AI 场景，产品分层和多样化 SKU 更合理。

性能参数和产品布局方面，Tom's Hardware 测试了两款 Venice 芯片：高密度 EPYC 9996 拥有 256 核和 512 线程，主打峰值吞吐性能；频率优化的 EPYC 9686F 则在 AI 主机节点角色中与 Nvidia Vera 正面竞争。AMD 还计划明年推出两个额外产品线：Venice-X 面向 HPC，配备 3D 堆叠缓存；Verano 则直接对标 Vera，作为 AI 主机节点，并采用 LPDDR5X 内存系统。文章指出，Nvidia Vera 在某些代理式负载的性能向量上确实表现较强，但 AMD 的测试结果支持其“产品组合优于单一 SKU”的论点。

技术影响和应用场景上，这场争论反映出代理式 AI 负载定义仍在演进。相比今年年初，业界现在更清楚代理循环如何工作，但“什么样的 CPU 最适合代理式 AI”的答案仍是“取决于具体任务”。AMD 的立场是：通用 CPU 通过核心密度、频率、缓存和内存配置的不同组合，可以覆盖编码代理、网页浏览代理、数据库查询代理、高并发沙箱多代理以及 HPC 等多种场景；而 Nvidia 和 Arm 的“专用 agentic CPU”叙事则面临负载多样性的挑战。总体来看，AMD 并未否认代理式 AI 的重要性，而是试图把竞争焦点从“是否专门设计”转向“能否用完整产品组合高效执行多样化代理工作流”。

items.title: AMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ deep dive and benchmarking
items.description: AMD has pulled back the curtain on its Zen 6 microarchitecture. We deep-dive into the differences between Zen 5 and 6, as well as detail our first benchmarks of AMD’s Venice CPUs.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter AMD’s EPYC ‘Venice’ CPUs are the first to debut the new Zen 6 architecture, and we’ve been testing two chips from the range over the past several weeks to see how they compare to Nvidia’s Vera, and more broadly, how the Zen 6 architecture departs from Zen 5 ahead of the expected consumer-focused Olympic Ridge launch next year. Zen 5 was a ground-up redesign of AMD’s storied Zen core, and Zen 6 takes that foundation and expands it in just about every regard.Zen 6 uses TSMC’s N2P node, but it also comes with significant architectural changes under the hood. Within the core, a redesigned vector engine pushes AMD’s SIMD performance even higher, and it now natively supports half-precision FP16 instructions alongside full, 32-bit precision. It also splits integer schedulers within the execution engine, allowing for more instructions in flight through the core.Across the die, AMD made other significant changes. The single IOD of previous generations is now split across two IODs, giving the SP7 platform access to 16 memory channels (though at the cost of PCIe 6.0 lanes compared to the previous generation and SP8 platform).Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The CCDs have been upgraded, too, for the first time since Zen 3. A standard Zen 6 CCD can now scale up to 12 cores, while a Zen 6c packs 32 cores. With Zen 5 and 5c, CCDs topped out at eight cores and 16 cores, respectively. For the Zen 6c CCD, AMD also doubled the amount of shared L3 per core, which effectively quadruples the L3 compared to Zen 5c, since the CCD packs twice the number of cores.Interestingly, Zen 6 is neither a marginal optimization to Zen 5, nor a complete architecture redesign. Stepping back, it looks like AMD pushes as many dials as it has access to to their highest level, and that holds up looking at performance. You may like AMD targets Nvidia with first official benchmarks for EPYC 'Venice' CPUs AMD drops an EPYC $15,000, 256-core beast Benchmarking Nvidia’s Vera CPU for the data center — standalone Vera tested against Granite Rapids-AP and EPYC Turin The 256-core EPYC 9996 delivers 1,024 threads in a 2P configuration, which came out 93% ahead of the 768-thread 2P EPYC 9965 server we tested in SPEC CPU 2026’s intrate throughput test. The frequency-optimized EPYC 9686F excels elsewhere, notably in scientific computing and HPC workloads, and it serves as AMD’s competitor to Vera, at least before the LPDDR-based Verano platform arrives from AMD next year.AMD says it believes Venice is fundamentally a generation ahead of the competition, which would be a worthless line if it wasn’t backed up by data. Intel’s Granite Rapids-AP is rarely in the conversation, and although Vera maintains some competitive positions, Venice is often ahead — sometimes orders of magnitude ahead.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsIntel’s Diamond Rapids is set to launch next year, which should help balance the scales. But AMD has set an incredibly high bar with Venice, one that it will likely extend even higher for some workloads with the arrival of Venice-X and Verano next year.There’s a lot to get to here. We have a full deep dive into the Zen 6 microarchitecture, a broader look at the chip itself, the platform(s) AMD is pushing out this generation, and of course, more than 100 benchmarks covering everything from Python performance to HPC.AMD Zen 6 microarchitecture breakdownAMD Zen 6 microarchitecture breakdown (Image credit: AMD)The headline for Zen 6 is a 27% average IPC uplift over Zen 5 in enterprise, cloud, and AI workloads. The debut of this new microarchitecture is focused on the data center, so you shouldn’t take that 27% IPC improvement as broadly applicable to all workloads. Additionally, AMD arrived at that number by comparing fixed-frequency Zen 5 to Zen 6c with 16 cores. As we’ll get into in the next section, a Zen 6c CCD can comfortably fit 16 Zen 6c cores with room to spare, while 16 Zen 5 cores are split across two CCDs. What to read next Leaked 256-core Zen 6c EPYC CPU destroys Zen 5 in early single-threaded benchmarks hints at 24% IPC gain Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’ The compute die is built on TSMC’s N2P node, which is an already optimized version of N2 that comes with a 5% performance improvement. Compared to N3E (Zen 5 used N4P), N2P offers an 18% speed improvement at iso-power, or a 36% reduction in power at the same speed. Swipe to scroll horizontally Row 0 - Cell 0 Speed Improvement (v. N3E) Power Improvement (v. N3E) Density (v. N3E) TSMC N2P +18% (iso-power) -36% (iso-speed) +15% AMD described Zen 5 as a ground-up redesign when the microarchitecture first broke cover in mid-2024, characterized by a wider execution engine capable of dispatching and returning eight instructions per cycle, a wider frontend to feed it, full AVX-512 support, and doubled bandwidth between the L2 and L1 cache. Zen 6 is a continuation of the redesign we saw on Zen 5. It carries many of the same characteristics, as well as the same general topology, just enhanced in a number of ways.As we go through the breakdown, keep in mind that Zen 6 and Zen 6c use the same microarchitecture. Zen 6c is just a space-optimized design that consumes less power, clocks lower, and, obviously, takes up less die space than a full Zen 6 core. But, the company uses the same microarchitecture inside the core, unlike Intel’s E-cores, which use a different microarchitecture than the P-cores. (Image credit: AMD)Starting with the frontend, it’s largely unchanged from Zen 5, short of a few notable improvements. You get the same dual 4-wide decode pipes and 8-dispatch, but AMD has improved the BPU and op cache. For the BPU, it has a 64-entry Return Address Stack, up from 52 on Zen 5. AMD also increased the op cache size back up to 6.75K entries from 6K on Zen 5 (Zen 4 also had a 6.75K-entry op cache). This larger cache can serve up to 18 micro-ops per cycle, up from 12 on Zen 5. (Image credit: AMD)AMD split the integer schedulers for Zen 6 (Zen 5 had a unified scheduler), now offering higher capacity, with 96 shared ALU/AGU and 48 dedicated ALU entries, compared to an 88 / 56 split for ALU/AGU on Zen 5. AMD also expanded the general-purpose registers to a 352-entry physical register file, up from 240 on Zen 5. (Image credit: AMD)The vector execution engine is also improved, following on the heels of a true 512-bit register in Zen 5. Zen 6 carries forward that 512-bit data path and adds some additional improvements. Notably, the engine now supports half-precision AVX-512 FP16 instructions, which needed to be converted in Zen 5’s vector execution engine. Also notable is the FP load/store bandwidth. Zen 5 supports two loads of any size, but Zen 6 supports either two 512-bit loads or four 256-bit loads. Store bandwidth is unchanged, at one 512-bit store or two 256-bit stores. (Image credit: AMD)Zen 6 carries forward the 48 KB 12-way L1 data cache from Zen 5, along with 1 MB 16-way private L2. The shared L3 is treated as victim cache for the L2, as is the case in Zen 5. However, AMD increased the in-flight window compared to Zen 5, with an 80-entry load queue and 128-entry store queue.AMD Zen 6 and Zen 6c CCD and platform breakdownAMD Zen 6 and Zen 6c CCD and platform breakdown (Image credit: AMD)Perhaps the biggest change going from Zen 5 to Zen 6 comes in the density of the CCD. Zen 6 offers up to 12 cores per CCD, up from 8 on Zen 5, while Zen 6c scales up to 32, double that of Zen 5c. Elsewhere, the updated CCDs either match or improve on Zen 5/5c CCDs.For Zen 6, AMD retained the 4 MB of L3 cache per core, increasing the total cache to 48 MB to accommodate the new 12-core limit. The maximum frequency of a standard Zen 6 CCD has increased from 5 GHz on Zen 5 to 5.3 GHz on Zen 6. Keep in mind these clocks are in the context of Venice; we expect higher maximum boost clocks on consumer Olympic Ridge.Zen 6c has more enhancements. AMD doubled the amount of L3 per core from 2 MB to 4 MB, matching the normal Zen 6 CCD. And, with double the L3 per core and double the number of cores, the Zen 6c CCD has a total of 128 MB of L3, quadruple that of a Zen 5c CCD. For Zen 6c, the maximum frequency is also up, going from 3.7 GHz on Zen 5c to 4.1 GHz on Zen 6c. (Image credit: AMD)Across both, AMD claims a “large core IPC uplift,” as well as improved power and SMT efficiency. We haven’t seen an overall IPC claim yet, though the numbers referenced above put Venice at about a 27% advantage over Turin in enterprise, cloud, and AI workloads. (Image credit: AMD)In the context of Venice, AMD can fit up to eight CCDs on a chip, coming out to 256 cores in total for Zen 6c, and 96 cores total for regular Zen 6 for SP7 platforms (the initial lineup for Venice). AMD is moving past the SP5 socket available to Genoa and Turin CPUs for SP7, which is a slightly larger socket at 76 x 80 mm (SP5 is ~72 x 75 mm). (Image credit: AMD)The topology of the chip is largely intact from Turin, short of the dual IO dies that characterize Venice. The two IODs live in the middle of the chip, flanked by Zen 6 CCDs. The second IOD is what gives SP7 chips access to 16 channels of memory per socket (8 channels per IOD), supporting up to 12,800 MT/s speeds using MRDIMMs in a 1DPC configuration. With RDIMMs, AMD supports up to 8,000 MT/s. The platform supports up to 8 TB of memory per socket, and AMD claims bandwidth of up to 1.6 TB/s per socket (1 TB/s per socket with RDIMMs).Also on the IOD, there’s the hardware root-of-trust, as well as AMD’s confidential computing extensions, including execution encryption, memory integrity, and trusted I/O. New to the platform is PCIe 6.0 at speeds up to 64 Gbps per lane. A 1P SP7 configuration has access to 96 PCIe 6.0 lanes, while a 2P platform has up to 128. Each configuration also comes with “bonus” PCIe 4.0 lanes, either 8 for 1P configs or 16 for 2P. (Image credit: AMD)Two 64G SerDes interfaces bring the PCIe lanes into the IOD, one of which is used to link the chips in a 2P configuration. That second interface can still optionally handle an additional 12 PCIe 6.0 lanes, giving the “up to” 128 2P lanes number. The bonus lanes run through a smaller 16G SerDes interface.Platforms with the SP8 socket trade memory channels for PCIe lanes. The SP8 socket is smaller at 62.5 x 80 mm, and the platform supports eight memory channels instead of 16, though with the same support for up to 12,800 MT/s MRDIMMs. Memory bandwidth drops to 819 GB/s for MRDIMMs and 512 GB/s for RDIMMs at the maximum supported transfer rate. (Image credit: AMD)However, SP8 chips have access to 64 PCIe 6.0 lanes per IOD, for a total of 128 lanes in a socket (plus the additional eight PCIe 4.0 bonus lanes). Just like SP7, some of those lanes are shared in a 2P configuration, dropping the total to 192 PCIe 6.0 lanes in 2P SP8 servers, with 16 additional PCIe 4.0 lanes. Both platforms support CXL 3.1. (Image credit: AMD)AMD also provided a platform breakdown for its upcoming Verano range, which uses the Zen 6 microarchitecture on an LPDDR5X-based platform, leveraging replaceable SOCAMM2 DIMMs.UPP, UBPS, and FAST in Zen 6 ‘Venice’ CPUsUPP, UBPS, and FAST in Zen 6 ‘Venice’ CPUs (Image credit: AMD)AMD has added a few quality-of-life features to Venice CPUs that should make them easier to manage when actually deployed. First is UPP, or Unified Power Provisioning, which is a power management feature that takes into account total platform power, allocating it as needed to different components, depending on the workload. With it, AMD says it’s able to deliver a power consumption of 830W on 16 servers to 706W on 18 servers, or a decrease in provisioned power by 15%, while increasing the number of servers per rack.Also dealing with power is UBPS, or Utilization Based Power Scaling. It’s a dynamic power scaling feature that aligns with whatever workload is running on the server, which AMD says “helps close the gap between provisioned and consumed power.” Like UPP, UBPS is concerned with platform power, not just the power consumption of the CPU. (Image credit: AMD)The most interesting addition is FAST, or Frequency Adaptive Spectrum Technology. The feature takes in telemetry from the platform and policies set in firmware to adjust the frequency within set power and thermal limits. It sounds a little more involved than a simple Precision Boost Overdrive for the data center, however.AMD described FAST to us as allowing for two performance tiers within one socket. As an example, AMD pointed to a 96-core Venice CPU, saying FAST allows 32 of those cores to run in a “premium” category, with a base clock of 3.65 GHz and a max clock of 5 GHz, while a “batch” category with 64 cores runs at 2 GHz with a 2.4 GHz max. AMD described it as multiple commercial SKUs within a single socket.Preliminary MEXT support, claims of 95% performance at 50% DRAM capacityPreliminary MEXT support, claims of 95% performance at 50% DRAM capacity (Image credit: AMD)Venice marks the point when AMD will start offering MEXT on its EPYC platforms. AMD aquired MEXT earlier this year, and it has used the feature internally. With HPE, AMD is rolling out “MEXT ready” platforms, which will, eventually, have access to MEXT licenses. The technology is interesting, especially given how constrained memory is right now.The general concept of MEXT is using flash as DRAM. Even the fastest flash is orders of magnitude slower than DRAM, but MEXT attempts to take advantage of DRAM access patterns to expose more memory to the system without it actually being there. Pages that haven’t been accessed in several minutes are offloaded to flash storage, and an AI model predicts pages that are needed. Then, those pages are loaded back into memory as you need them. (Image credit: AMD)Conceptually, it sounds too good to be true. AMD pointed out that MEXT is using a transformer-based LLM, and effectively, LLMs are predicting what words go next when generating text. Here, AMD says the bar isn’t even that high. As long as the model can stream the correct pages in, and do so fast enough to cover the flash latency, the order of them doesn’t matter.MEXT is delivered through a Linux kernel module, and AMD has bold claims about its capabilities. The company has deployed the software internally on 145 servers, which it expects to expand to over 2,000 servers next year. Currently, AMD is using it for critical EDA workflows, such as Synopsis PrimeTime. The company says that it’s able to maintain 95% of the application’s performance on Venice with just 50% of the system DRAM. Going down as low as 25%, the company claims the app maintains 80% of its performance. (Image credit: AMD)We’ll have more on MEXT shortly. The feature is exclusive to EPYC CPUs, and AMD was clear that it only applies to certain workloads right now. There are likely applications where you won’t be able to cut the DRAM capacity of a server, or where you’ll need to use a more conservative cut of 25% or less.AMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ test configurationsAMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ test configurationsAMD gave us access to two Zen 6 Venice systems for the purpose of testing, both of which were dual-socket servers. For the first system, we tested the dense EPYC 9996, which is AMD’s high-core-count design, packing 256 cores and 512 threads per socket, for a total of 512 cores and 1024 threads across a 2P system. It’s a peak throughput SKU, designed to handle heavily concurrent workloads.On the other end of the spectrum, we have the EPYC 9686F, which is still a high core count CPU in its own right, with 96 cores and 192 threads, giving a 2P system 192 cores and 384 threads. The “F” suffix for AMD’s data center CPUs notes a high-frequency SKU, designed to push performance up in more demanding applications, as opposed to the dense, frontend-focused EPYC 9996. The upcoming SP8 socket is focused on enterprise customers, with smaller core counts and support for fewer memory channels.Although the EPYC 9996 is a dense design with the Zen 6c core, it comes with a fairly high boost clock of 4.1 GHz, though a much lower 2.55 GHz base clock, which it will likely be running closer to in real deployments. It comes with a massive 1,024 MB pool of L3 for the chip, as well as a 600W rated TDP, though it can be manually adjusted between 400W and 600W.The EPYC 9686F proves out AMD’s claims about Venice, serving as one of two chips in the SP7 lineup to boost up to 5 GHz. It has a lower 500W TDP, though it can again run between 400W and 600W. This is the SKU AMD has heavily referenced in its published Venice benchmarks as a “96-core HF” model.It’s an interesting model, perhaps more so than the EPYC 9996. It’s in direct competition with Nvidia’s Vera CPU, not only based on core count, but also on performance. These two chips trade blows in several benchmarks, and it’s clear that AMD is pushing this SKU as its “agentic CPU” of the Venice lineup, similar to how Nvidia has positioned Vera. The Nigeria reference platform we tested these Zen 6 chips on came with top-end DDR5-12800 MRDIMMs, arranged to fully saturate the 16-channel memory with 32 sticks. This massive jump in memory support is a critical aspect of Venice, particularly for the hotly contested EPYC 9686F and its all-important matchup against Vera.Vera’s use of LPDDR5 SOCAMM2 memory allows for higher transfer rates than standard RDIMMs in a field-replaceable package, though through a relatively tame eight-channel setup. Vera can get away with 8-channel memory, however, with its topology allowing for massive data movement across the chip. AMD’s distributed design necessitates a bigger memory configuration, with double the channels and access to even higher transfer rates through the use of MRDIMMs.AMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ 9996 and 9686F SPEC estimatesAMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ 9996 and 9686F SPEC estimatesStarting off our benchmarks is SPEC CPU 2026, the de facto industry benchmark for server CPU performance. As usual with SPEC runs, the numbers below are “estimates.” We gathered the numbers from real SPEC runs, but we haven’t reported them to the SPEC committee, so they remain “estimates.”For the throughput benchmark suites, intrate and fprate, we ran a number of copies for each application equal to the thread count of the chip. All of our tests were run on Ubuntu Server 26.04 with Linux Kernel 7.0, and we used GCC 15.2 for all but the Venice chips. GCC 16 brings official support for Zen 6, which we used here. However, we did regression testing against GCC 15 and found only minor differences, and nothing that would change our standings.Using GCC 16 was important to keep our optimization flags equal. We used common GCC flags, including fast link-time optimization and march/mcpu flags to expose the correct processor instruction support. We also used the open-source jemalloc memory allocator across all tested systems. It has access to 1,024 threads in a 2P configuration, multiplying the clear speed improvements in Zen 6 broadly across more threads compared to last-gen’s top-end EPYC 9965. The 9996 scored a massive 93% higher in this test, though that number requires some context.Both throughput benchmarks in SPEC reward not only how much work is done, but also how quickly it’s done. With access to a much larger thread pool and improvements in Zen 6 broadly, there’s that multiplicative effect when looking at pure throughput. A 2P EPYC 9996 system is 93% faster than a 2P EPYC 9965 system in this benchmark, but not broadly across the board.The EPYC 9686F provides some context, which is still good news for AMD, just not on the level of doubling the performance of the previous generation. We unfortunately didn’t have access to a 9575F for a closer gen-on-gen comparison, but the EPYC 9755 is a decent proxy, with its 128 cores and relatively high 4.1 GHz boost clock. Compared with that CPU, the EPYC 9686F in a 2P configuration is 19% ahead — not too shabby considering the thread disadvantage.Critically for AMD, the EPYC 9686F is also 17% ahead of Nvidia’s Vera CPU. Rather, the EPYC 9696F is able to push up closer to the 9996, leaving both Zen 6 chips running circles around the field.AMD more than doubled the score with its Zen 6 chips compared to our Zen 5 touchpoints, which is a massive achievement. The EPYC 9686F excels even more over Vera in fprate with a 40% lead, despite only a minor bump in core count (88 on Vera to 96 on the 9686F). However, SPEC CPU also includes its speed suite, which looks at application performance when you can dedicate the whole chip to running just that one application, more along the lines of a client CPU benchmark.The EPYC 9686F naturally looks better here with its blistering 5 GHz boost clock. In the integer suite, the frequency-optimized chip is 21% ahead of Vera, both in a 2P configuration. The 9996 still holds up, only falling short of the 9686F, despite much more inter-CCD communication.SPEC shows the various improvements in Zen 6 showing up in a compounding fashion. There’s the new microarchitecture with an optimized vector path, but also more cores per CCD. And also support for higher memory speeds, as well as more memory channels. In isolation, any of these improvements are solid (if rote) for typical gen-on-gen improvements. Add them up in a workload that can take advantage of all of those improvements, however, and Zen 6 is blistering.AMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ 9996 and 9686F Python and memory benchmarksAMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ 9996 and 9686F Python and memory benchmarksTwo of the biggest performance vectors in the agentic era are memory performance and Python performance, at least at the moment. Agentic frameworks are largely defined by Python between LangGraph and CrewAI, though alternative frameworks written in TypeScript and Rust have started to appear as well. Regardless, Python remains important for agentic CPUs right now.Similarly, memory bandwidth is important for certain types of agents, particularly those that need to query large databases, regardless of if they’re a traditional relational database written in SQL or a non-relational database. However, this was with the OpenMP “true” policy for process binding, which binds processes to the thread they’re placed on to avoid them jumping around and skewing the results. Vera performs well, even with this policy, but its mesh cache and monolithic design allow it to realize big performance gains with the “spread” policy.This policy also binds processes, but it distributes them across the chip as far away from each other as possible. AMD chips don’t see an improvement with the spread policy, and Intel’s Granite Rapids-AP sees a slight regression. Vera, however, remains on top of the pile, with a clear victory margin with the policy applied. Starting with a broad overview, we have PyBench. Across the suite, the EPYC 9686F was 32% faster than Vera, while the EPYC 9996 naturally claims a smaller 14% lead with its relatively limited boost clocks. For gen-on-gen comparisons, the EPYC 9996 is an impressive 24% ahead of the EPYC, while the 9686F claims a lead of 35% over the 9755 – though, no small part of that advantage is the 900 MHz higher boost clock that the 9686F has access to. However, its poor decompression performance shows up even at level 3, and AMD takes over with a clear victory at the compression level 19, with Vera falling even further behind in decompression performance.The long mode results are especially interesting. Starting with LLVM, the frequency-optimized 9686F earns a top slot with makefiles, while the EPYC 9996 tops with Ninja. The drop is around 19% gen-on-gen, aligning with the performance we’ve seen with other workloads.In PHP, where Vera is more competitive, the EPYC 9686F squeezes out the most marginal of victories, but perhaps most telling is the 9996, which is in the upper tier of chips, despite how dense it is. Building applications, the Godot game engine and ImageMagick once again show both Venice chips on the top of the stack, outclassing the performance of Vera, which previously held a top slot in ImageMagick, and only fell slightly behind the 9755 in Godot. In CloverLeaf, the EPYC 9686F is more than twice as fast as Vera, and it’s nearly twice as fast with FFTE. In Octave, Vera retains its top position, but both Venice chips are only slightly behind.Although not traditional HPC, the heavily threaded number crunching behind the scenes in the Stockfish chess engine allows the 1,024 threads in a 2P EPYC 9996 server to outclass the 9965 by nearly 50%. Primesieve shows similarly large leaps, with the EPYC 9996 calculating some 37 billion prime numbers in less than half a second.More to comeMore to comeAMD already had a strong position in the newly reinvigorated CPU market with Turin. The unique topology and strong focus of Vera has allowed Nvidia to make inroads in certain workloads, but even looking at two SKUs from AMD’s broad Venice lineup, it’s clear that AMD is able to push performance much higher across the board. In some cases, that’s by orders of magnitude gen-on-gen.There isn’t one area of Zen 6, or the SoCs available with Venice broadly, that totally accounts for the performance increase. It’s small advantages throughout the design, pushing an already strong vector engine further, vastly increasing CCD density, and giving memory bandwidth a boon between support for 12,800 MT/s MRDIMMs and 16-channel memory courtesy of the dual IODs.But the story AMD has been trying to tell, and the one that’s difficult to ignore in the current market of a one-size-fits-all approach we’ve seen from Nvidia and Arm, is that Venice is available in a broad range of different configurations. We tested two chips on SP7, but the enterprise-focused SP8 socket is arriving within the next few months. And next year, AMD is pushing out Venice-X with 3D V-Cache for HPC workloads, as well as Verano, which looks like AMD’s take on Vera with its field-replaceable SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X memory.Even without those chips, the two SP7 chips we tested already give AMD a leading position among current data center CPUs. Intel’s Diamond Rapids could change that story come next year, but the EPYC 9686F provides top-tier performance with HPC and AI host node performance, while the EPYC 9996 provides unmatched throughput.MORE: Best CPUsMORE: CPU Benchmark HierarchyMORE: AMD vs. Intel

items.titleZh: AMD Zen 6 EPYC“Venice”深度剖析与基准测试
items.descriptionZh:
AMD 首批基于 Zen 6 架构的 EPYC“Venice”数据中心 CPU 已登场，Tom's Hardware 在数周内测试了两款双路平台芯片，重点对比 Nvidia 的 Vera CPU、AMD 上一代 Zen 5 EPYC，并借此观察 Zen 6 相对 Zen 5 的架构变化。Zen 5 曾被称为 AMD 对 Zen 核心的“从零重设计”，而 Zen 6 延续这一基础，在几乎每个维度上扩展：首发面向数据中心，消费级 Olympic Ridge 预计明年推出。AMD 声称 Venice 在代际上领先竞争对手，测试数据也显示其在多数负载中领先，部分项目差距可达数倍。产品路线方面，Venice 先用 SP7 平台打高核心数吞吐，随后还有面向企业的 SP8、明年的 Venice-X（带 3D V-Cache，面向 HPC）以及采用 LPDDR5X SOCAMM2 可更换内存的 Verano，后者更直接对标 Nvidia Vera 的 LPDDR 方案。Intel 的 Diamond Rapids 预计明年推出，可能改变竞争格局。

Zen 6 采用台积电 N2P 制程。相较 N3E，N2P 在同等功耗下速度提升 18%，或在同等速度下功耗降低 36%，密度提升 15%；Zen 5 使用的是 N4P。AMD 给出的核心指标是：在企业、云和 AI 负载中，Zen 6 相对 Zen 5 平均 IPC 提升 27%。但这一数字来自固定频率下 16 核 Zen 6c 与 Zen 5 的对比，不能简单外推到所有负载。微架构上，前端基本延续 Zen 5 的双 4 宽解码和 8 发射，但分支预测返回地址栈从 52 项增至 64 项，op cache 从 6K 增至 6.75K 项，每周期可提供最多 18 个微操作（Zen 5 为 12）。整数执行引擎将调度器拆分，容量提高为 96 项共享 ALU/AGU 加 48 项专用 ALU（Zen 5 为 88/56），物理通用寄存器文件从 240 项增至 352 项，使更多指令可在核心内同时在途。向量引擎是重点：在 Zen 5 的 512 位数据通路基础上，Zen 6 原生支持 AVX-512 FP16 半精度指令，而 Zen 5 需要转换；加载带宽支持两个 512 位加载或四个 256 位加载，存储仍为一个 512 位或两个 256 位。缓存方面保留 48KB 12 路 L1 数据缓存、1MB 16 路私有 L2，L3 作为 L2 的 victim cache，但加载队列增至 80 项、存储队列增至 128 项。

CCD 密度是 Zen 6 的另一大变化。标准 Zen 6 CCD 从 Zen 5 的 8 核提升到最多 12 核，Zen 6c CCD 从 16 核翻倍到 32 核；Zen 6 每核保留 4MB L3，总 L3 达 48MB，最高频率从 5GHz 升至 5.3GHz（Venice 语境，消费级可能更高）；Zen 6c 每核 L3 从 2MB 翻倍到 4MB，总 L3 达 128MB，是 Zen 5c CCD 的四倍，最高频率从 3.7GHz 升至 4.1GHz。Zen 6c 与 Zen 6 使用同一微架构，只是面积和功耗优化、频率较低，不同于 Intel E-core 采用不同微架构。芯片层面，Venice 把过去单个 IOD 拆成两个 IOD，使 SP7 平台每插槽获得 16 个内存通道（每 IOD 8 通道），支持 1DPC 下 12,800 MT/s 的 MRDIMM，RDIMM 最高 8,000 MT/s，每插槽最大 8TB 内存，MRDIMM 带宽最高 1.6TB/s，RDIMM 为 1TB/s；代价是相较上代和 SP8 平台，PCIe 6.0 通道数有所取舍。SP7 的 1P 配置有 96 条 PCIe 6.0 通道，2P 最多 128 条，另有 8/16 条 PCIe 4.0 附加通道；SP8 插槽更小，改为 8 内存通道，MRDIMM 带宽 819GB/s、RDIMM 512GB/s，但每 IOD 有 64 条 PCIe 6.0，单插槽共 128 条，2P 服务器最多 192 条 PCIe 6.0 加 16 条 PCIe 4.0。两平台均支持 CXL 3.1。SP7 最多可放 8 个 CCD，Zen 6c 配置达 256 核，标准 Zen 6 配置达 96 核。

Venice 还加入几项部署管理特性。UPP（统一功耗供给）从整平台角度按负载分配功耗，AMD 称可把 16 台服务器的 830W 功耗配置优化为 18 台 706W，配置功耗降低 15% 并增加每机架服务器数。UBPS（基于利用率的功耗缩放）根据实际负载动态调功耗，缩小“配置功耗”和“实际消耗功耗”的差距。FAST（频率自适应频谱技术）结合平台遥测和固件策略，在功耗与热限制内调频，可在同一插槽内划分两个性能层级：例如 96 核 Venice 中 32 核以 3.65GHz 基础、5GHz 最高运行，64 核以 2GHz 基础、2.4GHz 最高运行，相当于单插槽内提供多种商业 SKU。MEXT 则是 AMD 今年收购并首次在 EPYC 平台推出的“闪存当 DRAM”方案：把数分钟未访问的页面卸载到闪存，用基于 Transformer 的模型预测所需页面并预取回内存，通过 Linux 内核模块交付。AMD 与 HPE 推“MEXT ready”平台，内部已在 145 台服务器使用，明年计划扩至 2000 多台，主要用于 EDA 等关键工作流；其称在 Synopsis PrimeTime 中仅用 50% 系统 DRAM 可保持 95% 性能，降到 25% DRAM 仍保持 80%。不过该技术目前只适用于特定负载，并非所有应用都能大幅削减内存。

测试平台为两套双路 Venice 系统。EPYC 9996 是密集吞吐型 Zen 6c SKU：每路 256 核/512 线程，2P 共 512 核/1024 线程，2.55GHz 基础、4.1GHz 加速，1024MB L3，600W TDP（可在 400–600W 调整）。EPYC 9686F 是高频型：每路 96 核/192 线程，2P 共 192 核/384 线程，3.4GHz 基础、5GHz 加速，384MB L3，500W TDP（400–600W 可调），被 AMD 作为对标 Nvidia Vera 的“agentic CPU”。测试平台使用 32 条 64GB DDR5-12800 MRDIMM（2TB），对比平台包括 EPYC 9965/9755 配 DDR5-6000 RDIMM、Xeon 6980P 配 DDR5-8800，以及 Nvidia Vera 配 16 条 96GB LPDDR5-9600 SOCAMM2（1.5TB）。在 SPEC CPU 2026 的 intrate 吞吐测试中，2P EPYC 9996 比 2P EPYC 9965 高 93%，但部分来自线程数翻倍的乘数效应；9686F 比 9755 高 19%，比 Vera 高 17%。fprate 浮点吞吐中，Zen 6 两款芯片相对 Zen 5 对照点得分翻倍以上，9686F 比 Vera 高 40%（96 核对 88 核）。SPEC speed 整数单应用测试中，5GHz 的 9686F 比 Vera 高 21%。Python 方面，PyBench 中 9686F 比 Vera 高 32%，9996 高 14%；代际上 9996 比 9965 高 24%，9686F 比 9755 高 35%，部分受益于高 900MHz 加速频率。内存 STREAM 在 OpenMP“true”绑定策略下 AMD 比 Vera 高 11%–19%，但 Vera 在“spread”策略下凭借网格缓存和单体设计大幅领先；MBW 小数组时 9996 略胜 Vera，大数组时 Vera 第一，说明 AMD 用 16 通道和 12,800 MT/s MRDIMM 缩小了差距，但 Vera 内存子系统仍有优势。

其他负载中，压缩方面 AMD 在 zstd 和 7-Zip 总体领先；Vera 在低压缩级别起步较快，但解压性能较弱，长时间模式下差距更明显。Blender 渲染中 9996 比 9965 快 30%–40%，Barbershop 场景快 35%；9686F 以一半核心匹配 9965。Vera 因无原生 Arm 版未参与 Blender。C-Ray 中 Vera 仍居首，但双 9996 接近；OSPRay 中 AMD 明显领先，9996 在环境光遮蔽和科学可视化中约为 Xeon 6980P 和 Vera 的三倍，dim_512 测试进一步体现新向量引擎和内存带宽。Java SciMark 中 9686F 综合分比 Vera 高 92%，9996 比 9965 高 24%，但 FFT 单项 Vera 第一。ClickHouse 列式数据库中，Vera 冷缓存即可维持性能，x86 需暖缓存；暖缓存后 9686F 领先，9996 相对 9965 因核心数过大出现缓存一致性回退。simdjson 再次体现 Venice 向量引擎优势。编译负载中，LLVM 的 makefiles 由 9686F 夺冠、Ninja 由 9996 夺冠；PHP 中 9686F 微弱胜 Vera；Godot 和 ImageMagick 中两款 Venice 均领先。HPC 方面，9686F 在 CloverLeaf 中比 Vera 快两倍以上，FFTE 接近两倍；Octave 中 Vera 仍第一但 Venice 紧随；Stockfish 中 2P 9996 比 9965 快近 50%；Primesieve 中 9996 不到 0.5 秒算出约 370 亿个素数。

总体看，Zen 6 并非 Zen 5 的边际优化，也不是彻底推翻重来，而是把 Zen 5 已铺好的基础在向量引擎、CCD 密度、内存通道与频率等可调维度上推到更高。性能提升不是单一因素，而是新微架构、更多每 CCD 核心、更高内存速率和更多通道叠加的结果。AMD 凭借 Turin 已在数据中心 CPU 市场占据强势位置，Venice 进一步扩大领先；Nvidia Vera 依靠独特拓扑在内存、冷缓存和部分单项中保持竞争力，但在大量通用数据中心负载中，Venice 两款 SKU 已展现全面优势，9686F 适合 HPC 和 AI 主机节点，9996 适合极致吞吐。其影响在于：在 agentic AI 推动 CPU 需求回暖、内存容量成为瓶颈的背景下，AMD 用广泛 SKU、SP7/SP8 平台、MEXT 内存扩展和明年的 Venice-X/Verano 形成组合拳，直接挑战 Nvidia 和 Arm 的“一刀切”方案；但 Intel Diamond Rapids 明年到来，竞争仍未定局。

items.title: Alice Huang reportedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI GPU imports during three-year relationship with Jensen Huang
items.description: Alice Huang is reportedly connected to a web of Chinese companies, which then leveraged her closeness to Jensen Huang to gain access to billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia GPUs.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is also suspected of being a spy working for the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS). Now, an investigation by The Information has revealed a 'labyrinth' of companies centered around Shanghai Century Litong and connected to Singaporean firm Megaspeed, which has previously been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. The report claims Alice Huang helped move 240,000 banned chips into the country, mostly H100 and H200 systems, and was instrumental in securing AI GPU imports to the tune of $7.5 billion.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedSources in the report link the two companies to Alice Huang via their personal knowledge and corporate registration records, while there have also been reports that some of the Nvidia AI chips Megaspeed bought went to Shanghai Century Litong’s data centers in China. But aside from these corporate ties, there were also numerous reports about Ms. Huang’s personal relationship with the Nvidia chief, and how it gave her the ability to procure chips that were otherwise hard to get elsewhere.Ms. Huang allegedly boasted about her access to the Nvidia CEO publicly. People familiar with her said that she regularly uploaded photos with Jensen to her WeChat account and even shared other images with customers to establish her credibility. She even claimed that Jensen Huang would often celebrate her birthday with dinner and gifts, while an Nvidia China sales employee said that she was a familiar face at the company’s annual event for local Chinese partners.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: When AI shipments hit delays or faced some trouble, Ms. Huang allegedly would step in to get them moving through the supply chain again. One other person who knows her said that she would often cite her close relationship with Nvidia and its suppliers as the reason why she could always get Nvidia AI chips. It’s estimated that $4.6 billion worth of AI chips have been imported through Megaspeed from 2023 to 2025, with another $2 billion routed through Speedmatrix. It was also reported that Shanghai Century Litong bought GPUs from other sources, with the assistance of Alice Huang if the orders faced an issue, with the total value of the GPUs acquired estimated to be around $7.5 billion. The report claims Ms. Huang helped move some 240,000 banned chips into China.Alice Huang may have appeared in Jensen Huang’s circle much earlier than previously believed. One source told the publication that Kang Wei, Alice Huang’s husband, met Jensen Huang during the 2010s, when Nvidia was primarily a PC gaming GPU manufacturer. According to the report, Kang Wei was a private equity investor focusing on videogame companies back then. In contrast, Ms. Huang reportedly worked for two media companies in China, although some say that there were no records of her doing so. She eventually jumped into banking and finance, working at HSBC and then CITIC Securities, before finally entering the data center industry in 2023 with Megaspeed’s pivot and the founding of Shanghai Century Litong. You may like US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to Congress over affair with alleged Chinese spy Shanghai Century Litong is a data center operator founded in June 2023 by a shareholder that was ultimately under the control of Huang Yu, the sister of Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le. The company then provided compute capacity to AI tech giants in China, including Alibaba, Tencent, and other smaller labs. A few months after its founding, it received coveted Nvidia Preferred Cloud Partner status in October 2023, which is an important milestone as Nvidia requires anyone with this status to have demonstrated sufficient capability in handling and running Nvidia hardware as well as generating revenue at a certain level, although that threshold varies by region and partner type.In exchange for this, partners get better access to Nvidia’s limited number of chips, which became crucial for Shanghai Century Litong as the China-specific A800 and H800 chips were banned for sale to China around the same period. Although the move immediately banned the sales of these GPUs from Nvidia, it did not affect the chip stocks that were already in the hands of distributors. This meant that Shanghai Century Litong had priority access to the limited supply of these AI GPUs as Nvidia’s preferred partner.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsMegaspeed, on the other hand, was reportedly owned by a company called Huang Le Limited and led by Ms. Huang when it pivoted in 2023 and was subsequently sold to Singaporean entity Swiftdata soon after this. Megaspeed then set up a subsidiary called Speedmatrix, which has two offices in Johor, Malaysia, a couple of months after that. The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the U.S. agency in charge of monitoring export control compliance, noted that the Nvidia hardware found in Speedmatrix data centers was still in its boxes when they inspected the sites, triggering a deeper investigation into the company. Still, it’s been alleged that Nvidia intervened in the BIS probe, with the company retaining its Nvidia partner status to this day.Despite her public closeness with the Nvidia chief, she’s rather elusive when it comes to her personal information. Two other people said that she has always been vague about what she does at her companies, and that she’s careful when it comes to signing documents and leaving a paper trail that could easily be followed. Still, the Chinese embassy denies any links to Alice Huang, even as the FBI looks into the situation. items.titleZh: 据报道，Alice Huang在与黄仁勋三年交往期间，为促成逾75亿美元英伟达AI GPU进口发挥关键作用
items.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware援引The Information的调查报道称，英伟达CEO黄仁勋被指承认与Megaspeed高管Alice Huang存在婚外情，而Alice Huang同时被怀疑为中国国家安全部（MSS）工作的间谍。报道围绕上海世纪利通（Shanghai Century Litong）和新加坡公司Megaspeed梳理出一个复杂的公司网络，并称Megaspeed此前已被指控走私价值20亿美元的英伟达芯片。该报道还声称，Alice Huang协助将约24万颗被禁运芯片运入中国，其中以H100和H200系统为主，并促成约75亿美元AI GPU进口。相关说法主要来自报道及消息人士，中国大使馆否认Alice Huang与中方有关联，FBI正在调查此事。

公司关系方面，上海世纪利通是一家2023年6月成立的数据中心运营商，其股东最终由Alice Huang的姐姐Huang Yu控制；该公司为中国AI企业提供算力，客户包括阿里巴巴、腾讯及其他较小实验室。成立数月后，上海世纪利通于2023年10月获得英伟达“首选云合作伙伴”（Preferred Cloud Partner）资格。Megaspeed则由Huang Le Limited持有、由Alice Huang领导，2023年转型后不久被出售给新加坡实体Swiftdata；Megaspeed随后在马来西亚柔佛设立子公司Speedmatrix并设两个办公室。美国工业与安全局（BIS）检查时发现Speedmatrix数据中心的英伟达硬件仍未开箱，从而引发更深入调查。报道还称，英伟达曾干预BIS调查，并使该公司至今保留英伟达合作伙伴资格。

这一事件的核心机制之一是英伟达的云合作伙伴资格与出口管制之间的衔接。Preferred Cloud Partner要求企业展示部署和运行英伟达硬件的能力，并达到一定收入门槛，具体标准因地区和伙伴类型而异；作为回报，合作伙伴能更优先获得英伟达有限的芯片供应。上海世纪利通获得该资格时，正值美国禁止对华销售中国特供的A800和H800芯片。该禁令立即禁止英伟达销售这些GPU，但不影响分销商手中已有的库存，因此作为英伟达优先合作伙伴的上海世纪利通，得以优先获得这些受限AI GPU的有限供应。H100/H200则属于更高端、受控更严的AI芯片，报道称相关芯片通过Megaspeed、Speedmatrix等渠道流入中国。

金额和规模方面，报道估计2023年至2025年间，通过Megaspeed进口的AI芯片价值约46亿美元，另有约20亿美元通过Speedmatrix转运；上海世纪利通还从其他渠道购买GPU，若订单出现问题会由Alice Huang协助推进，相关GPU总价值估计约75亿美元。报道称Alice Huang曾公开炫耀自己与黄仁勋的关系，定期在微信上传与黄的合影，并向客户展示其他照片以建立可信度；她还声称黄仁勋常与她共进晚餐庆祝生日并送礼。一名英伟达中国销售员工称，她是英伟达中国合作伙伴年度活动上的熟面孔。当AI芯片出货延迟或遇到问题时，她据称会介入推动供应链恢复，并常以自己与英伟达及其供应商的密切关系解释为何总能拿到英伟达AI芯片。

报道还追溯了Alice Huang更早的圈子。消息人士称，她的丈夫Kang Wei在2010年代认识黄仁勋，当时英伟达主要是一家PC游戏GPU厂商，Kang Wei则是关注视频游戏公司的私募股权投资人。Alice Huang据称曾在中国两家媒体公司工作，但也有人说没有相关记录；她后来进入银行金融业，先后任职于汇丰和中信证券，最终在2023年随着Megaspeed转型和上海世纪利通成立进入数据中心行业。尽管她与黄仁勋关系公开密切，但两名知情人士称，她一直对自己在公司中的具体角色含糊其辞，签署文件和留下可追踪纸质记录时也相当谨慎。

items.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
items.description: Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA […]
items.content: Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell, an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate, an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine, NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot. These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future. Securing AI Agents in the Open NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF puts security infrastructure for autonomous agents in the community’s hands to build, inspect and improve — accelerating development and hardening its safeguards. “The cloud-native community has a new infrastructure challenge: giving agents secure environments in which to operate,” said Jim Zemlin, CEO of the Linux Foundation. “NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF gives developers a shared foundation to build on and an opportunity to shape how agent security evolves. Bringing this work into the community enables broader collaboration on infrastructure that will be critical to the next generation of cloud-native applications.” OpenShell gives organizations control over what AI agents can do. It applies deterministic controls to agent activity, so teams can enforce policies as agents use tools, access inference services and execute workloads. Its extensible architecture lets teams connect their own compute, inference providers, credential storage and monitoring tools. This allows organizations to apply governance across different deployment environments while integrating OpenShell with their existing enterprise systems. Hundreds of organizations have put OpenShell to use, and the project has received tens of thousands of contributions in less than a year since launch. Scaling Agent Execution on Kubernetes Governing agents is only part of the challenge. Organizations also need to deploy them at scale. NVIDIA is contributing to Agent Substrate, a Google-originated project in the CNCF Sandbox, and ensuring it works with NVIDIA Dynamo for model inference and KAI Scheduler for shared cluster resource allocation. This effort brings together agent execution, inference serving and resource scheduling on Kubernetes. Agent Substrate preserves agent environments between tasks while releasing compute when agents are idle. By suspending and resuming those environments across a shared pool of agents, it lets teams scale agent workloads without keeping dedicated compute running for every session. NVIDIA and Google are also collaborating on an integration of OpenShell and Agent Substrate, so enterprises can secure and govern agents across clouds and on-premises systems. Building an Open Foundation for AI Factories AI factories need to offer customers managed Kubernetes services while retaining control of their infrastructure, software and customer experience. Three new open source projects extend the DSX AI Factory Platform to make Kubernetes easier to run and inference faster to scale. The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform software stack, from GPU infrastructure and Kubernetes management to workload orchestration and model serving. NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) — now available in public preview — provide open source building blocks for delivering managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure. They automate cluster lifecycle management and provide signed, version-pinned images. NVKE and NVKR are launching with ecosystem support that extends their reach across AI infrastructure platforms and cloud services. Mirantis, Netris, OpenNebula Systems, Rafay, Spectro Cloud and vCluster, together with Firmus and SK Telecom, have aligned with NVIDIA on integration plans to bring NVKE and NVKR capabilities into their offerings. NVIDIA Snapshot addresses the challenge of bringing additional inference capacity online quickly. Loading models and warming up workloads can delay scaling and recovery. The open source, modular component restores checkpointed replicas in seconds, without model reload or warmup, supporting faster startup, recovery and elasticity for inference and agentic workloads on Kubernetes. Design partners Crusoe and Saturn Cloud have evaluated Snapshot on their own workloads using NVIDIA HGX B300 systems. Crusoe, an upstream contributor to Snapshot, tested GLM-5.3 on Crusoe Cloud and reduced the time for the workload to become ready from roughly eight minutes to 31 seconds. Saturn Cloud, a token factory platform, benchmarked Snapshot for scale-from-zero inference and reduced vLLM startup times from between two and 8.5 minutes to six and 34 seconds. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at KubeCon.

items.titleZh: 英伟达通过捐赠 OpenShell 及全新 AI 基础设施扩大开源承诺
items.descriptionZh:
Kubernetes作为管理数千个AI工厂中应用运行的开源系统，已成为AI的基础支撑，且对其需求持续增长。在KubeCon + CloudNativeCon这一Kubernetes与云原生社区旗舰大会上，NVIDIA宣布深化其开源承诺，将自主AI代理的安全与治理开源运行时NVIDIA OpenShell贡献给云原生计算基金会（CNCF）。作为CNCF沙箱项目，OpenShell将由将其集成到产品中的组织共同治理，并借助全球安全专家的力量得到强化。NVIDIA还参与贡献了Google主导的开源框架Agent Substrate，用于在Kubernetes上大规模运行长时运行的代理工作负载，该项目已被CNCF沙箱接纳。此外，NVIDIA发布了NVIDIA DSX AI Factory平台的新组件：NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine、NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes和NVIDIA Snapshot，帮助团队在Kubernetes上部署、管理和扩展GPU基础设施。这些进展共同推动Kubernetes成为大规模AI工作负载的领先基础，赋能开发者构建更安全、更高效的AI基础设施。

在代理安全保障方面，NVIDIA将OpenShell贡献给CNCF，把自主代理的安全基础设施交到社区手中，加速开发并强化防护措施。Linux基金会CEO Jim Zemlin表示，云原生社区面临新的基础设施挑战——为代理提供安全的运行环境，NVIDIA的贡献为开发者提供了共享基础，并让他们有机会塑造代理安全的演进方向。OpenShell让组织能够控制AI代理的行为，对代理活动施加确定性控制，使团队能够在代理使用工具、访问推理服务和执行工作负载时执行策略。其可扩展架构允许团队接入自己的计算、推理提供商、凭证存储和监控工具，从而在不同部署环境中实施治理，并与现有企业系统集成。已有数百家组织使用OpenShell，该项目在发布不到一年内收到数万次贡献。

在Kubernetes上扩展代理执行方面，NVIDIA参与贡献了源自Google的CNCF沙箱项目Agent Substrate，并确保其与NVIDIA Dynamo（用于模型推理）和KAI Scheduler（用于共享集群资源分配）协同工作，将代理执行、推理服务和资源调度整合在Kubernetes上。Agent Substrate在任务之间保留代理环境，同时在代理空闲时释放计算资源，通过在共享代理池中挂起和恢复这些环境，使团队能够扩展代理工作负载，而无需为每个会话保持专用计算运行。NVIDIA和Google还在合作集成OpenShell与Agent Substrate，使企业能够跨云和本地系统保护和治理代理。

在构建AI工厂的开放基础方面，AI工厂需要为客户提供托管Kubernetes服务，同时保持对基础设施、软件和客户体验的控制。三个新的开源项目扩展了DSX AI Factory平台，使Kubernetes更易于运行，推理扩展更快速。NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine和NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes现已提供公开预览版，为在GPU基础设施上交付托管Kubernetes服务提供开源构建模块，自动化集群生命周期管理并提供签名、版本固定的镜像。Mirantis、Netris、OpenNebula Systems、Rafay、Spectro Cloud和vCluster，以及Firmus和SK Telecom已与NVIDIA就集成计划达成一致，将NVKE和NVKR能力引入其产品。NVIDIA Snapshot解决快速增加推理容量的问题，模型加载和工作负载预热会延迟扩展和恢复，这一开源模块化组件可在数秒内恢复检查点副本，无需重新加载模型或预热，支持Kubernetes上推理和代理工作负载的更快启动、恢复和弹性。设计合作伙伴Crusoe和Saturn Cloud已在各自工作负载上使用NVIDIA HGX B300系统评估Snapshot。Crusoe作为Snapshot的上游贡献者，在Crusoe Cloud上测试GLM-5.3，将工作负载就绪时间从约8分钟缩短至31秒。Saturn Cloud对Snapshot进行从零扩展推理的基准测试，将vLLM启动时间从2至8.5分钟缩短至6至34秒。

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature

items.content: Google is rolling out its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, to the general public after releasing it to a select group of “cybersecurity defenders” two weeks ago. Google claims Carbon is its “strongest model” yet, and capable of competing with the very best systems from Anthropic and OpenAI.Google says Gemini 4 Carbon “pushes the frontier even further” than Argon, referring to the company’s other frontier model that launched only last month. The company said Argon will likely remain “the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work,” but that Carbon is “built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence,” such as complex, multi-step coding and open-ended scientific research.To highlight Carbon’s utility for long-horizon work involving AI agents, Google said it is also previewing a “swarm” feature on its agentic development platform Antigravity, which will let users turn a single prompt “into a coordinated team of agents.”Carbon is rolling out today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, Google said in a blog post. It will also be available to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, the AI Mode in Search, and on Antigravity. It is not clear when — or if — Carbon will be available to lower tier subscribers or free users.As with the launch of Argon, Google is pricing Carbon very competitively. The model is launching with an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and a quarter the cost of Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model, which launched yesterday. Even after those costs double at the end November — when the introductory period of lower prices finishes — Carbon will still be significantly cheaper than frontier rivals on a per-token basis, though this doesn’t necessarily translate to lower costs as models can use different numbers of tokens for the same tasks.Benchmarks cited by Google when it first announced Carbon suggest the model is one of the most powerful on the market across most metrics, behind Fable 5.2. It should be noted that companies can and do cherry-pick benchmark results to show their tools in the best possible light.The release, hot on the heels of Argon, marks a decisive return for Google at the very forefront of AI research. For months, frontier development looked like a two-horse race between Anthropic and OpenAI.
