history.titleZh: 据报道，Alice Huang在与黄仁勋三年交往期间，为促成逾75亿美元英伟达AI GPU进口发挥关键作用
history.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware援引The Information的调查报道称，英伟达CEO黄仁勋被指承认与Megaspeed高管Alice Huang存在婚外情，而Alice Huang同时被怀疑为中国国家安全部（MSS）工作的间谍。报道围绕上海世纪利通（Shanghai Century Litong）和新加坡公司Megaspeed梳理出一个复杂的公司网络，并称Megaspeed此前已被指控走私价值20亿美元的英伟达芯片。该报道还声称，Alice Huang协助将约24万颗被禁运芯片运入中国，其中以H100和H200系统为主，并促成约75亿美元AI GPU进口。相关说法主要来自报道及消息人士，中国大使馆否认Alice Huang与中方有关联，FBI正在调查此事。

公司关系方面，上海世纪利通是一家2023年6月成立的数据中心运营商，其股东最终由Alice Huang的姐姐Huang Yu控制；该公司为中国AI企业提供算力，客户包括阿里巴巴、腾讯及其他较小实验室。成立数月后，上海世纪利通于2023年10月获得英伟达“首选云合作伙伴”（Preferred Cloud Partner）资格。Megaspeed则由Huang Le Limited持有、由Alice Huang领导，2023年转型后不久被出售给新加坡实体Swiftdata；Megaspeed随后在马来西亚柔佛设立子公司Speedmatrix并设两个办公室。美国工业与安全局（BIS）检查时发现Speedmatrix数据中心的英伟达硬件仍未开箱，从而引发更深入调查。报道还称，英伟达曾干预BIS调查，并使该公司至今保留英伟达合作伙伴资格。

这一事件的核心机制之一是英伟达的云合作伙伴资格与出口管制之间的衔接。Preferred Cloud Partner要求企业展示部署和运行英伟达硬件的能力，并达到一定收入门槛，具体标准因地区和伙伴类型而异；作为回报，合作伙伴能更优先获得英伟达有限的芯片供应。上海世纪利通获得该资格时，正值美国禁止对华销售中国特供的A800和H800芯片。该禁令立即禁止英伟达销售这些GPU，但不影响分销商手中已有的库存，因此作为英伟达优先合作伙伴的上海世纪利通，得以优先获得这些受限AI GPU的有限供应。H100/H200则属于更高端、受控更严的AI芯片，报道称相关芯片通过Megaspeed、Speedmatrix等渠道流入中国。

金额和规模方面，报道估计2023年至2025年间，通过Megaspeed进口的AI芯片价值约46亿美元，另有约20亿美元通过Speedmatrix转运；上海世纪利通还从其他渠道购买GPU，若订单出现问题会由Alice Huang协助推进，相关GPU总价值估计约75亿美元。报道称Alice Huang曾公开炫耀自己与黄仁勋的关系，定期在微信上传与黄的合影，并向客户展示其他照片以建立可信度；她还声称黄仁勋常与她共进晚餐庆祝生日并送礼。一名英伟达中国销售员工称，她是英伟达中国合作伙伴年度活动上的熟面孔。当AI芯片出货延迟或遇到问题时，她据称会介入推动供应链恢复，并常以自己与英伟达及其供应商的密切关系解释为何总能拿到英伟达AI芯片。

报道还追溯了Alice Huang更早的圈子。消息人士称，她的丈夫Kang Wei在2010年代认识黄仁勋，当时英伟达主要是一家PC游戏GPU厂商，Kang Wei则是关注视频游戏公司的私募股权投资人。Alice Huang据称曾在中国两家媒体公司工作，但也有人说没有相关记录；她后来进入银行金融业，先后任职于汇丰和中信证券，最终在2023年随着Megaspeed转型和上海世纪利通成立进入数据中心行业。尽管她与黄仁勋关系公开密切，但两名知情人士称，她一直对自己在公司中的具体角色含糊其辞，签署文件和留下可追踪纸质记录时也相当谨慎。

history.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
history.description: Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA […]
history.content: Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell, an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate, an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine, NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot. These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future. Securing AI Agents in the Open NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF puts security infrastructure for autonomous agents in the community’s hands to build, inspect and improve — accelerating development and hardening its safeguards. “The cloud-native community has a new infrastructure challenge: giving agents secure environments in which to operate,” said Jim Zemlin, CEO of the Linux Foundation. “NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF gives developers a shared foundation to build on and an opportunity to shape how agent security evolves. Bringing this work into the community enables broader collaboration on infrastructure that will be critical to the next generation of cloud-native applications.” OpenShell gives organizations control over what AI agents can do. It applies deterministic controls to agent activity, so teams can enforce policies as agents use tools, access inference services and execute workloads. Its extensible architecture lets teams connect their own compute, inference providers, credential storage and monitoring tools. This allows organizations to apply governance across different deployment environments while integrating OpenShell with their existing enterprise systems. Hundreds of organizations have put OpenShell to use, and the project has received tens of thousands of contributions in less than a year since launch. Scaling Agent Execution on Kubernetes Governing agents is only part of the challenge. Organizations also need to deploy them at scale. NVIDIA is contributing to Agent Substrate, a Google-originated project in the CNCF Sandbox, and ensuring it works with NVIDIA Dynamo for model inference and KAI Scheduler for shared cluster resource allocation. This effort brings together agent execution, inference serving and resource scheduling on Kubernetes. Agent Substrate preserves agent environments between tasks while releasing compute when agents are idle. By suspending and resuming those environments across a shared pool of agents, it lets teams scale agent workloads without keeping dedicated compute running for every session. NVIDIA and Google are also collaborating on an integration of OpenShell and Agent Substrate, so enterprises can secure and govern agents across clouds and on-premises systems. Building an Open Foundation for AI Factories AI factories need to offer customers managed Kubernetes services while retaining control of their infrastructure, software and customer experience. Three new open source projects extend the DSX AI Factory Platform to make Kubernetes easier to run and inference faster to scale. The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform software stack, from GPU infrastructure and Kubernetes management to workload orchestration and model serving. NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) — now available in public preview — provide open source building blocks for delivering managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure. They automate cluster lifecycle management and provide signed, version-pinned images. NVKE and NVKR are launching with ecosystem support that extends their reach across AI infrastructure platforms and cloud services. Mirantis, Netris, OpenNebula Systems, Rafay, Spectro Cloud and vCluster, together with Firmus and SK Telecom, have aligned with NVIDIA on integration plans to bring NVKE and NVKR capabilities into their offerings. NVIDIA Snapshot addresses the challenge of bringing additional inference capacity online quickly. Loading models and warming up workloads can delay scaling and recovery. The open source, modular component restores checkpointed replicas in seconds, without model reload or warmup, supporting faster startup, recovery and elasticity for inference and agentic workloads on Kubernetes. Design partners Crusoe and Saturn Cloud have evaluated Snapshot on their own workloads using NVIDIA HGX B300 systems. Crusoe, an upstream contributor to Snapshot, tested GLM-5.3 on Crusoe Cloud and reduced the time for the workload to become ready from roughly eight minutes to 31 seconds. Saturn Cloud, a token factory platform, benchmarked Snapshot for scale-from-zero inference and reduced vLLM startup times from between two and 8.5 minutes to six and 34 seconds. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at KubeCon.
history.author: Warren Barkley
history.titleZh: 英伟达通过捐赠 OpenShell 及全新 AI 基础设施扩大开源承诺
history.descriptionZh:
Kubernetes作为管理数千个AI工厂中应用运行的开源系统，已成为AI的基础支撑，且对其需求持续增长。在KubeCon + CloudNativeCon这一Kubernetes与云原生社区旗舰大会上，NVIDIA宣布深化其开源承诺，将自主AI代理的安全与治理开源运行时NVIDIA OpenShell贡献给云原生计算基金会（CNCF）。作为CNCF沙箱项目，OpenShell将由将其集成到产品中的组织共同治理，并借助全球安全专家的力量得到强化。NVIDIA还参与贡献了Google主导的开源框架Agent Substrate，用于在Kubernetes上大规模运行长时运行的代理工作负载，该项目已被CNCF沙箱接纳。此外，NVIDIA发布了NVIDIA DSX AI Factory平台的新组件：NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine、NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes和NVIDIA Snapshot，帮助团队在Kubernetes上部署、管理和扩展GPU基础设施。这些进展共同推动Kubernetes成为大规模AI工作负载的领先基础，赋能开发者构建更安全、更高效的AI基础设施。

在代理安全保障方面，NVIDIA将OpenShell贡献给CNCF，把自主代理的安全基础设施交到社区手中，加速开发并强化防护措施。Linux基金会CEO Jim Zemlin表示，云原生社区面临新的基础设施挑战——为代理提供安全的运行环境，NVIDIA的贡献为开发者提供了共享基础，并让他们有机会塑造代理安全的演进方向。OpenShell让组织能够控制AI代理的行为，对代理活动施加确定性控制，使团队能够在代理使用工具、访问推理服务和执行工作负载时执行策略。其可扩展架构允许团队接入自己的计算、推理提供商、凭证存储和监控工具，从而在不同部署环境中实施治理，并与现有企业系统集成。已有数百家组织使用OpenShell，该项目在发布不到一年内收到数万次贡献。

在Kubernetes上扩展代理执行方面，NVIDIA参与贡献了源自Google的CNCF沙箱项目Agent Substrate，并确保其与NVIDIA Dynamo（用于模型推理）和KAI Scheduler（用于共享集群资源分配）协同工作，将代理执行、推理服务和资源调度整合在Kubernetes上。Agent Substrate在任务之间保留代理环境，同时在代理空闲时释放计算资源，通过在共享代理池中挂起和恢复这些环境，使团队能够扩展代理工作负载，而无需为每个会话保持专用计算运行。NVIDIA和Google还在合作集成OpenShell与Agent Substrate，使企业能够跨云和本地系统保护和治理代理。

在构建AI工厂的开放基础方面，AI工厂需要为客户提供托管Kubernetes服务，同时保持对基础设施、软件和客户体验的控制。三个新的开源项目扩展了DSX AI Factory平台，使Kubernetes更易于运行，推理扩展更快速。NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine和NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes现已提供公开预览版，为在GPU基础设施上交付托管Kubernetes服务提供开源构建模块，自动化集群生命周期管理并提供签名、版本固定的镜像。Mirantis、Netris、OpenNebula Systems、Rafay、Spectro Cloud和vCluster，以及Firmus和SK Telecom已与NVIDIA就集成计划达成一致，将NVKE和NVKR能力引入其产品。NVIDIA Snapshot解决快速增加推理容量的问题，模型加载和工作负载预热会延迟扩展和恢复，这一开源模块化组件可在数秒内恢复检查点副本，无需重新加载模型或预热，支持Kubernetes上推理和代理工作负载的更快启动、恢复和弹性。设计合作伙伴Crusoe和Saturn Cloud已在各自工作负载上使用NVIDIA HGX B300系统评估Snapshot。Crusoe作为Snapshot的上游贡献者，在Crusoe Cloud上测试GLM-5.3，将工作负载就绪时间从约8分钟缩短至31秒。Saturn Cloud对Snapshot进行从零扩展推理的基准测试，将vLLM启动时间从2至8.5分钟缩短至6至34秒。

history.content: Google is rolling out its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, to the general public after releasing it to a select group of “cybersecurity defenders” two weeks ago. Google claims Carbon is its “strongest model” yet, and capable of competing with the very best systems from Anthropic and OpenAI.Google says Gemini 4 Carbon “pushes the frontier even further” than Argon, referring to the company’s other frontier model that launched only last month. The company said Argon will likely remain “the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work,” but that Carbon is “built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence,” such as complex, multi-step coding and open-ended scientific research.To highlight Carbon’s utility for long-horizon work involving AI agents, Google said it is also previewing a “swarm” feature on its agentic development platform Antigravity, which will let users turn a single prompt “into a coordinated team of agents.”Carbon is rolling out today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, Google said in a blog post. It will also be available to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, the AI Mode in Search, and on Antigravity. It is not clear when — or if — Carbon will be available to lower tier subscribers or free users.As with the launch of Argon, Google is pricing Carbon very competitively. The model is launching with an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and a quarter the cost of Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model, which launched yesterday. Even after those costs double at the end November — when the introductory period of lower prices finishes — Carbon will still be significantly cheaper than frontier rivals on a per-token basis, though this doesn’t necessarily translate to lower costs as models can use different numbers of tokens for the same tasks.Benchmarks cited by Google when it first announced Carbon suggest the model is one of the most powerful on the market across most metrics, behind Fable 5.2. It should be noted that companies can and do cherry-pick benchmark results to show their tools in the best possible light.The release, hot on the heels of Argon, marks a decisive return for Google at the very forefront of AI research. For months, frontier development looked like a two-horse race between Anthropic and OpenAI.
history.author: Robert Hart
history.titleZh: 谷歌发布具备智能体“蜂群”功能的Gemini 4 Carbon
history.descriptionZh:
Google 正式向公众推出最新 AI 模型 Gemini 4 Carbon。该模型两周前曾先向一组“网络安全防御者”开放，如今扩大至更广泛用户。Google 称 Carbon 是其“最强模型”，能够与 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的最顶尖系统竞争。此次发布距离 Google 上月推出另一款前沿模型 Argon 仅隔不久，被视为 Google 在经历一段由 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 主导的“双雄竞赛”后，决定性地重返 AI 研究最前沿。

从产品定位看，Carbon 并非简单替代 Argon，而是面向更高难度智能任务的旗舰模型。Google 表示，Carbon 比 Argon“进一步推进前沿”，后者预计仍将是“大多数软件工程和知识工作的理想选择”，而 Carbon 则“为测试模型智能极限的任务而构建”，例如复杂的多步骤编程和开放式科学研究。原文未披露 Carbon 的具体架构细节，但从官方描述看，其核心创新在于更强的高难度推理与长时程任务能力，并服务于 AI 代理执行复杂工作流。为突出这一点，Google 还在其代理式开发平台 Antigravity 上预览“swarm”功能，允许用户将单个提示转化为“一个协调工作的代理团队”，从而支持多代理协同完成长周期任务。

发布渠道方面，Carbon 即日起通过 Google AI Studio 中的 Gemini API 以及面向企业的 Gemini for business 向所有付费开发者和企业开放；同时向所有 Google AI Ultra 订阅者提供，覆盖 Gemini 应用、搜索中的 AI Mode 以及 Antigravity。至于较低档订阅用户或免费用户何时能用、是否能用，目前尚不明确。

性能与价格是此次发布的重要看点。Google 为 Carbon 设定了极具竞争力的 introductory 价格：每百万输入 token 2 美元、每百万输出 token 10 美元，约为 OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 成本的五分之一、Anthropic 昨日发布的 Fable 5.2 模型的四分之一。即便在 11 月底优惠期结束、价格翻倍后，Carbon 按 token 计算仍将显著便宜于前沿竞争对手。不过，按 token 单价低并不必然意味着总使用成本更低，因为不同模型完成同一任务所需的 token 数量可能不同。Google 首次公布 Carbon 时引用的基准测试显示，该模型在大多数指标上处于市场最强之列，但落后于 Fable 5.2；同时需要指出，企业通常会挑选有利于自己的基准结果来展示产品优势。

技术影响和应用场景上，Carbon 主要面向需要极限智能的复杂多步骤编码、开放式科研、长时程代理任务和多代理协同开发。其通过 Gemini API、企业平台和 Ultra 订阅多渠道开放，可能进一步降低开发者在高难度任务中使用前沿模型的门槛，并对 Anthropic、OpenAI 形成直接价格与能力竞争。结合 Antigravity 的 swarm 预览，Google 也在强化“从单提示到代理团队”的代理式开发叙事，瞄准未来 AI 代理协作和自动化工作流市场。总体来看，Carbon 的发布不仅补齐了 Google 在前沿模型竞争中的位置，也显示出其试图以高能力、低价格和多代理工具链组合争夺开发者和企业客户。

history.title: Going deep on local AI performance benchmarking with Apple’s Mac Studio with M5 Ultra taking on Nvidia DGX Spark
history.description: But if you're thinking about dropping over $10K for the purpose of building a local AI inference setup, is a Mac Studio right for you?
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Apple’s updated Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra SoC has already proven itself as one of the most powerful systems around, thanks to its 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU with Neural Accelerators for the matrix math operations that drive AI compute. Beyond that raw power, options for up to 512GB of unified memory have many local AI enthusiasts lining up for the 13 to 15 weeks it’ll take for Apple to ship one right now.But is our tested Mac Studio config worth a whopping $12,300 or more for those folks? We already tested the maxed-out M5 Ultra chip with the popular Qwen 3.8 27B in our initial review, but that compact dense model doesn’t come anywhere close to exercising 256GB of memory. We wanted to fill that pool to the brim with cutting-edge large models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM 5.3 Flash.We also have some new benchmarks at our disposal to see how the Mac Studio stacks up in agentic tasks on the GPU side in the wake of our review of the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia’s RTX Spark chip. So there's much to dig into.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Agentic AI performance and power efficiencyWe started our more detailed local AI testing with Artificial Analysis' AgentPerf-Local benchmark. This test plays back recorded inference traces with certain models across a range of agentic AI workloads to gauge performance. Artificial Analysis provides a full breakdown of this workload, but the bulk of its work takes place in prompt processing rather than token generation. As a result, it should favor systems with lots of raw compute, which both GB10 and the M5 Ultra have at their disposal.The M5 Ultra's 80-core GPU dwarfs GB10's 48 Blackwell SMs at a high level. Even without detailed info on clocks, it would be extremely difficult for GB10 to outgun the M5 Ultra in this test. And the Mac's 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth gives it just over four times as much decode bandwidth as GB10's 273 GB/s. But as our past tests have shown, raw specs aren't as important as delivered performance with AI. Delivered performance can vary greatly from paper specs. You may like Apple Mac Studio (M5 Ultra) review: Local model citizen outpaces DGX Spark and Threadripper Benchmarking Qwen 3.8 27B on RTX 5090 and beyond Nvidia introduces 64GB DGX Spark to throw local AI fans a lifeline amid the RAMpocalypse We continued to use the dense Qwen 3.8 27B for this test. We used llama.cpp as our inference backend on both the Mac Studio and a single Dell Pro Precision GB10 box, which is nearly identical to the DGX Spark. We further enabled Qwen 3.8 27B’s native multi-token prediction (MTP) support for a decode speed boost on both platforms. (Image credit: Future)Versus a single DGX Spark-like system, the M5 Ultra Mac Studio finishes this agentic test in just under half the time, an extremely impressive result. One might think this is a silly comparison given the imbalance in compute resources and memory bandwidth between these two systems, but the cost of a single 4TB Dell Pro Precision GB10, like the one we tested, is now a whopping $10K, so comparing it to the $12K Mac Studio head-to-head isn’t actually that far-fetched.Because AgentPerf-Local performs a fixed amount of work on every system, we can also directly compare power efficiency between platforms by recording the wall power consumed by a single Spark and the Mac Studio and converting it to task energy in kilojoules. (Image credit: Future)At least with llama.cpp, the Mac Studio not only finishes the AgentPerf-Local test much faster than the DGX Spark, but it also consumes less task energy overall — about 16% less. A different inference engine might produce a more favorable result for the Spark-like system, but apples-to-apples, this test looks fantastic for the Mac Studio.We can multiply both task time and energy consumed (in kilojoules) together to arrive at the energy-delay product (EDP) for each system. A lower EDP wraps up a fast time to completion and a low task energy into a single comparable figure for efficiency. What to read next We tested the RTX Spark Superchip in Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra Sipeed reveals Chinese-made DGX Spark and Ryzen AI Halo rival, expected to cost $3,999 Apple Mac mini (Late 2026) Review: Strong performance, but losing its grip on value (Image credit: Future)The Mac Studio’s EDP is under half that of the DGX Spark in this test, once again indicating its impressive efficiency and performance with this dense model and workload.Going big with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM 5.3 FlashOf course, Qwen 3.8 27B doesn’t need 256GB (or even 128GB) of RAM to do its thing. To really stretch the legs of the Mac Studio, we chose two larger open models that are near the top of capability benchmarks right now: GLM-5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017.The M5 Ultra Mac Studio can natively fit quantized versions of these models (a four-bit quantization in the case of GLM 5.3 and a two-bit quantization courtesy of Unsloth for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) in its 256GB of RAM, but there’s no way even those quantizations will fit on a single 128GB DGX Spark.That’s where the clustering capability of Nvidia’s platform comes in. We’ve already seen how pairing up Sparks can scale up one’s local inference capacity, and that capability is critical when evaluating them against a Mac Studio like this.But the rapidly rising prices of GB10 systems have frustrated our value analysis during the course of this testing. For just one example, Lenovo set all of its ThinkStation PGX systems to a “coming soon” status during our tests. And as we’ve already mentioned, the Dell Pro Precision GB10s we’re clustering here are an eye-popping $10K each. We have no reason to believe the rest of the GB10 systems on the market will be that much cheaper once this current volatility shakes out.No matter how you slice it, getting even a pair of DGX Sparks with 4TB SSDs is going to end up costing quite a bit more than this single Mac Studio, even if $20K for a dual-Dell cluster is at the top end of the market. $15K or more is a relatively more reasonable benchmark, but even then, that’s 25% more money than a single M5 Ultra Studio.We don't yet have end-to-end agentic tests for these larger models, but directionally, we can still consider prompt processing and decode performance to see which of these systems would deliver faster agentic turnaround.Because of the limited choice of compatible inference engines for Apple Silicon, we have to use llama.cpp for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. Worse, the Mac Studio can't hold both the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 model weights and the DSpark speculative decoding model required to boost token output even with a two-bit quantization, so we’re forced to leave performance on the table.In contrast, the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash serving recipe for our Spark cluster can take advantage of DSpark speculative decoding and the TensorFold inference engine, which can deliver higher performance than llama.cpp. Image 1 of 4 (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) Image 1 of 4 View Original Image 2 of 4 View Original Image 3 of 4 View Original Image 4 of 4 View Original Even with MLX support, llama.cpp performance with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on the Mac Studio is pokey next to the DGX Spark cluster. Between its slower prompt processing speed and unaugmented decoding, it would end up at a disadvantage in agentic work with this model.The community two-Spark serving recipe from Mia’s AI Lab with TensorFold is a major asset for owners of those systems, even accounting for the bit of extra work involved in setting up and managing a Spark cluster.Where the Mac running llama.cpp needs anywhere from 10 to 25 minutes to digest the longest context lengths we tested for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the Spark cluster needs under five minutes at most to do the same jobs with this recipe — and the TensorFold inference engine is much faster on the decode side, too. If you want to run this model locally, a pair of Sparks is the clear winner right now.With DeepSeek out of the way, let’s consider GLM 5.3 Flash, another leading open model for local intelligence. Because MTP with GLM 5.3 Flash doesn't require a separate drafting model, we can give it a decode boost on the Mac Studio without the memory headroom issues we saw with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. For our Spark cluster, we chose to run GLM 5.3 Flash using a recipe cooked up by Mia's AI Lab. Image 1 of 4 (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) Image 1 of 4 View Original Image 2 of 4 View Original Image 3 of 4 View Original Image 4 of 4 View Original GLM 5.3 Flash runs much better on llama.cpp than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash does, but even so, the DGX Spark cluster delivers much faster prompt processing times across the board. The M5 Ultra's memory bandwidth advantage means the Mac is delivering higher tokens per second on the decode side, but it’s likely that any agentic turn would still finish faster on the Spark cluster.Because a TensorFold serving recipe is available for GLM 5.3 Flash on Apple Silicon, however, we can see just how much extra performance is available from an MLX-specific four-bit model quantization and a theoretically higher-performance inference engine. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original This serving recipe turbocharges the Mac Studio’s performance compared to llama.cpp. Prompt processing times with TensorFold get much closer to those of the Spark cluster, and decode throughput is a startling three times faster, on average.We expect (and can only hope) that improved inference engine support and serving recipes for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 on the M5 Ultra will arrive in time as community members unleash their coding agents on this hardware, because the performance potential is clearly there for Apple Silicon.Bottom lineA single M5 Ultra Mac Studio can deliver incredible local AI performance and power efficiency versus a single DGX Spark when all the puzzle pieces fall into place. And that's not as absurd a comparison as it might seem.Prices for unified memory systems are ballooning to the point that a single Dell Pro Precision GB10 system with a 4TB SSD is now over $10K, closing in on the $12K-ish price of the Mac Studio configuration that we tested. We expect those trends will only continue as the RAM and NAND supply crunch becomes more acute.But our broader experience shows that the M5 Ultra's impressive performance isn't assured from every model and inference engine, especially from the bigger and highly intelligent models you'll want to put in 256GB of RAM.This Mac's prompt processing speeds can really rip with llama.cpp and smaller models like Qwen 3.8 27B, but you really want to ensure that you have a higher-performance serving recipe at your disposal for bigger models like GLM 5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. The TensorFold engine runs GLM 5.3 Flash incredibly well, but it doesn’t support DeepSeek at all yet.As we emphasized in our review of the M4 Max Mac Studio, memory bandwidth is just one factor in AI inference performance. You need to take the entire hardware-software stack into account in order to wholly judge the performance and model compatibility available from these extremely pricey unified memory setups.Even as Apple closes the performance shortfalls of its hardware for AI inference, development and support around the MLX stack has a ways to go before it catches up with the maturity and performance, as well as the model and inference engine options, available on Nvidia hardware.The enduring value of the DGX Spark platform beyond its raw performance and scalability is that the breadth and velocity of community software development and support around the platform has gotten to the point that you're virtually assured of a way to run a hot new model soon after its weights hit Hugging Face (at least assuming you have enough Sparks to cluster to provide the memory capacity necessary).That assurance of community software support and ongoing development, along with the DRAM and NAND supply crunches, means high demand and ever higher prices for 128GB GB10 boxes. Two such Sparks with 4TB drives will run you an eye-watering $15K to $20K+, depending on the partner system and storage configuration you choose. And those prices are likely to continue rising, making a single Mac Studio a potentially appealing option as long as Apple doesn’t jack up its prices for these systems in turn.If strong local AI performance is just one thing you need from a personal workstation, and you also want one of the world's fastest CPUs and a powerful GPU for general-purpose work in one well-rounded, efficient, and quiet compact chassis, the Mac Studio is a remarkable system.If you can wait for software to catch up to this system’s incredible performance potential for local AI and don’t mind the possibility of narrower model and inference engine support compared to a DGX Spark setup, get in line, as lead times for these systems stretch into February 2027 as of this writing.But if you're thinking about dropping well over $10K specifically for the purpose of building a local AI inference setup right now, perhaps for yourself or a small office, clustering a pair of Sparks gets you both the memory capacity and compute horsepower you need with the robust software support and broad model compatibility you’d expect for that outlay to be worthwhile. Those assurances may be worth the lower raw performance potential of such a cluster compared to the Mac Studio.

history.titleZh: 深入探讨本地AI性能基准测试：Apple Mac Studio搭载M5 Ultra挑战Nvidia DGX Spark
history.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware 对苹果新款 Mac Studio（M5 Ultra SoC）的本地 AI 实测显示，这台机器在合适软件栈下已能与英伟达 DGX Spark/GB10 平台正面竞争，但其性能释放高度依赖模型、量化方式和推理引擎支持。M5 Ultra 配备 36 核 CPU、80 核 GPU，GPU 内集成面向 AI 计算所需矩阵运算的 Neural Accelerators，并可选最高 512GB 统一内存；测试配置价格约 1.23 万美元以上，当前发货等待期达 13 到 15 周，文章称交付时间甚至排到 2027 年 2 月。

测试背景是：此前用 Qwen 3.8 27B 这类紧凑稠密模型做初始评测，远未吃满 256GB 内存，因此本次改用 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 和 GLM 5.3 Flash 等前沿大模型填充内存池，并引入 Artificial Analysis 的 AgentPerf-Local 基准。该基准回放真实推理轨迹，覆盖多种智能体式 AI 工作负载，工作量固定，且主要耗时在 prompt processing（提示处理/预填充）而非 token generation（逐 token 生成），因此更偏重原始算力。M5 Ultra 的 80 核 GPU 在规格上远超 GB10 的 48 个 Blackwell SM；其 1.2TB/s 内存带宽约为 GB10 273GB/s 的四倍，理论上解码带宽优势明显。但文章强调，AI 实际交付性能可能与纸面规格差距很大。

在 Qwen 3.8 27B 测试中，Mac Studio 和单台 Dell Pro Precision GB10（与 DGX Spark 几乎相同）均使用 llama.cpp，并启用 Qwen 原生多 token 预测（MTP）提升解码速度。结果显示，M5 Ultra Mac Studio 完成 AgentPerf-Local 智能体测试的时间不到单台 Spark 类系统的一半；由于工作量固定，还可直接比较能耗：Mac Studio 不仅更快，总任务能耗还低约 16%。将任务时间和能耗相乘得到能量延迟积（EDP），Mac Studio 的 EDP 不到 DGX Spark 的一半，说明其在该稠密模型和工作负载下兼具高性能与高能效。文章认为，单台 4TB Dell Pro Precision GB10 售价已高达约 1 万美元，与约 1.2 万美元的 Mac Studio 对比并不离谱。

在大模型测试中，M5 Ultra 的 256GB 统一内存可原生容纳量化后的 GLM 5.3 Flash（4-bit）和 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017（Unsloth 2-bit），而单台 128GB DGX Spark 无法容纳，必须靠集群扩展内存容量。不过 GB10 系统价格快速上涨：测试用 Dell Pro Precision GB10 每台约 1 万美元，联想 ThinkStation PGX 一度显示“即将推出”；两台带 4TB SSD 的 Spark 集群约需 1.5 万至 2 万美元以上，比单台 M5 Ultra Studio 贵 25% 以上。文章指出，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 在 Mac 上只能用 llama.cpp，且 Mac 无法同时容纳模型权重和 DSpark 投机解码模型（即便 2-bit 量化），性能受限；双 Spark 集群则可用 DSpark 投机解码和 TensorFold 推理引擎，社区服务配方来自 Mia's AI Lab。实测中，Mac 用 llama.cpp 处理最长上下文需 10 到 25 分钟，Spark 集群用该配方最多不到 5 分钟，解码侧也更快，因此若专门本地运行 DeepSeek，双 Spark 当前明显胜出。

GLM 5.3 Flash 的情况不同：其 MTP 不需要单独草稿模型，Mac 可在不牺牲内存余量的情况下获得解码加速。用 llama.cpp 时，GLM 在 Mac 上比 DeepSeek 表现好，但 Spark 集群的 prompt processing 仍全面更快；M5 Ultra 凭借内存带宽在解码 tokens/s 上更高，但智能体单轮任务仍可能由 Spark 集群更快完成。关键变数是 Apple Silicon 已有 GLM 5.3 Flash 的 TensorFold 服务配方，可使用 MLX 专用 4-bit 量化和更高性能推理引擎。相比 llama.cpp，TensorFold 使 Mac 的 prompt processing 大幅接近 Spark 集群，解码吞吐平均快约三倍。文章期待 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 也出现更好的推理引擎和服务配方，因为 Apple Silicon 的性能潜力明显存在。

结论是：单台 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 在软硬件条件齐备时，相对单台 DGX Spark 可提供惊人的本地 AI 性能和能效；但并非每个模型和推理引擎都能保证这种表现，尤其是放入 256GB 内存的大模型。llama.cpp 搭配 Qwen 3.8 27B 等较小模型时，Mac 的 prompt processing 很快；但 GLM 5.3 Flash、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 等大模型需要高性能服务配方。TensorFold 跑 GLM 5.3 Flash 很好，但尚不支持 DeepSeek。文章重申，内存带宽只是 AI 推理性能的一个因素，必须看完整软硬件栈；苹果硬件在 AI 推理上的短板在缩小，但 MLX 生态的成熟度、性能以及模型和推理引擎选择仍落后英伟达。DGX Spark 平台的长期价值在于社区软件开发广度和速度，新模型权重发布后通常很快有运行方案，前提是集群内存足够。DRAM 和 NAND 供应紧张推高 128GB GB10 系统需求和价格，两台 4TB Spark 约 1.5 万至 2 万美元以上且可能继续上涨，这反而使单台 Mac Studio 更具吸引力，只要苹果不跟进涨价。若本地 AI 只是个人工作站需求之一，同时还需要世界级 CPU、强大通用 GPU、均衡高效安静的紧凑机箱，Mac Studio 是出色系统；若能等待软件生态追上其本地 AI 潜力，且不介意模型和推理引擎支持面较窄，可以排队购买。但若现在专门投入超过 1 万美元搭建本地 AI 推理环境，例如个人或小办公室使用，集群两台 Spark 能同时提供所需内存容量和算力，并拥有更稳健的软件支持与广泛模型兼容性，这种保障可能值得接受其相对 Mac Studio 更低的原始性能潜力。

history.title: President Trump says the FBI is investigating Jensen Huang’s affair
history.description: The FBI is probably concerned about the implication of a Chinese agent having influence over the leader of the U.S.'s leading AI chip manufacturer.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As more information about the ongoing situation at Nvidia unravels, U.S. President Donald Trump has confirmed that the FBI is investigating CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy days after he admitted to the indiscretion. According to the Associated Press, the president said this during a briefing at the White House, with one reporter asking him about his knowledge of Huang’s issue before it became publicly known. The news comes amidst a separate bombshell report from Bloomberg, which claims that Nvidia intervened in a US government probe of suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed, where Alice Huang was an executive.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained“Well, I’ve been hearing about it, and I’ve been reading about it over a period of time, but, uh, not too long ago,” Trump said. “We’ll look into, I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something, and I think he’ll be in good shape.” He also said, “I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling alright, how you’re doing. He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”It has been previously reported that U.S. intelligence services suspected that Alice Huang, who previously held an executive position at Megaspeed, had ties to the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS), which is one of the country’s intelligence services, and that they told the President about it over a year ago. However, it was reported he did not act on the information, as he reportedly did not want to jeopardize Nvidia sales or antagonize Beijing, especially after the White House approved the export of H200 chips to China with an attached 25% fee.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Congress has called Huang once to confront him about these rumors, with the CEO confirming his affair with Alice Huang shortly after. The committee said it has "concerns over Nvidia’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company.” Now, it seems that the FBI, which is the U.S.’s primary domestic counterintelligence agency, is looking into the situation, too.While the infidelity of tech executives is usually outside the purview of politicians and law enforcement, Jensen Huang’s sensitive position as the head of the leading AI chip manufacturer that arguably single-handedly drove the global AI race has made him a prominent target. China has denied the accusation that Alice Huang is its agent, but a think tank suggests that “China is employing ‘attractive women’ posing as investors, business professionals, academics, or romantic partners to gain access to U.S. tech talent, networks, and research infrastructure.” You may like US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to having an affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims This is why Nvidia’s supposed intervention in the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security’s (BIS) investigation into Megaspeed is becoming a concern. Megaspeed has been investigated for allegedly smuggling $2 billion worth of Nvidia AI processors into China, although Nvidia has claimed that it has done its due diligence and did not find any signs of diversions by the company. Despite that, Bloomberg reports that Nvidia executive vice president and general counsel Tim Teter reached out to U.S. Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security and BIS head Jeffrey Kessler to ask about the administration’s investigation into the company and whether the BIS was involved in Singapore’s detention of Alice Huang at that time. Sources claimed that the U.S. agency was not involved in Ms. Huang’s apprehension by Singaporean authorities.The publication reported BIS staff were told to route all Nvidia requests through Kessler or to seek approval from him for any outreach involving the company, which people say was highly unusual, and that Teter even supposedly reached out directly to BIS employees. When the affected employees forwarded the emails to Kessler and raised their concerns, the BIS chief instructed them to handle the case by the book. But in late 2025, the Justice Department, which was working alongside the BIS, asked the bureau to pause its efforts on the Megaspeed investigation.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsEven though Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, who was linked to Megaspeed and is suspected to be working at the behest of Beijing, there is still no clear proof that Ms. Huang had a direct role in influencing the Nvidia chief to push for the resumption of Nvidia AI chip sales to China. Still, the unraveling of this supposed spy plot has caught the attention of the American leadership, and they’re now asking questions about Nvidia’s security protocols and the company’s sway on Washington. history.titleZh: 特朗普总统称联邦调查局正在调查黄仁勋的婚外情
history.descriptionZh:
美国总统特朗普已确认，美国联邦调查局（FBI）正在调查英伟达CEO黄仁勋与疑似中国间谍Alice Huang的婚外情。此前黄仁勋已承认这段关系。特朗普在白宫简报会上表示，他“一段时间以来”听到并读到相关消息，并称FBI正在“就某事进行调查”，但他认为黄仁勋“状况会不错”。特朗普还称当天与黄仁勋通话，黄表示自己“完全不知道”对方是间谍。

事件背景涉及美国情报界对Alice Huang的怀疑。此前有报道称，美国情报机构怀疑曾任Megaspeed高管的Alice Huang与中国国家安全部（MSS）有关联，并在一年多前向总统通报。但据报道，特朗普当时未采取行动，部分原因是担心影响英伟达销售或激怒北京，尤其是在白宫批准向中国出口H200芯片并附加25%费用之后。美国国会曾就相关传闻质询黄仁勋，黄随后承认与Alice Huang的婚外情。国会委员会表示，担忧英伟达“针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议”，以及黄仁勋与一家新加坡数据中心公司中“与中国情报有关联的高管”的关系。FBI作为美国国内反情报主要机构，现已介入调查。中国否认Alice Huang是中方特工，但有智库称中国利用“有吸引力的女性”伪装成投资者、商务人士、学者或恋爱对象，以接触美国技术人才、网络和研究基础设施。

与此同时，彭博社报道称，英伟达干预了美国政府针对Megaspeed涉嫌芯片走私的调查。Megaspeed被调查涉嫌将价值20亿美元的英伟达AI处理器走私到中国。英伟达称已进行尽职调查，未发现该公司转移产品的迹象。报道指出，英伟达执行副总裁兼总法律顾问Tim Teter曾联系美国商务部负责工业与安全事务的副部长、工业与安全局（BIS）负责人Jeffrey Kessler，询问政府对Megaspeed的调查，以及BIS是否参与新加坡当时对Alice Huang的拘留。消息人士称，BIS并未参与新加坡当局对Alice Huang的拘捕。彭博社还称，BIS员工被要求将英伟达的所有请求转交Kessler，或就涉及该公司的外联寻求其批准，这种做法被认为“极不寻常”；Teter还曾直接联系BIS员工。受影响的员工将邮件转发给Kessler并表达担忧后，Kessler指示按章处理。但到2025年底，与BIS协同工作的美国司法部要求BIS暂停对Megaspeed的调查。

从产业和技术影响看，这则新闻的核心并非芯片架构或性能参数，而是英伟达高端AI芯片出口管制、供应链安全和政企关系。H200是英伟达面向数据中心AI训练和推理的高端加速器，美国批准其对华出口并附加25%费用，使英伟达处于美中科技竞争和出口管制的敏感位置。Megaspeed案则涉及价值20亿美元的AI处理器可能被转运至中国，凸显先进AI芯片在出口管制下的走私与 diversion 风险。英伟达作为全球领先AI芯片厂商，其安全协议、游说活动和与华盛顿的互动正受到更严格审视。

目前，尚无明确证据证明Alice Huang直接影响黄仁勋推动恢复对华AI芯片销售，但这一疑似间谍案及英伟达干预调查的报道已引发美国领导层关注。事件涉及反情报、出口执法、企业治理和美国对华芯片政策的多重交叉，后续FBI调查、BIS与司法部对Megaspeed案的处理，以及国会是否进一步审查英伟达的安全协议和对华盛顿的影响力，将成为观察重点。原文未披露H200具体性能参数或与其他芯片的对比数据，新闻焦点集中在安全与政策层面。

history.title: Law firm files class-action lawsuit against Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang confirms affair with alleged Chinese spy
history.description: Class-action lawsuit and legal investigations against Nvidia over securities fraud start flying
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 16 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The baying of the hounds can be heard at a distance. Yesterday, Nvidia's Jensen Huang confirmed that it was indeed true that he had a romantic affair with Alice Huang (not related to the family), who U.S. intelligence services claim is a Chinese honeypot tasked with facilitating smuggling of the firm's advanced GPUs into China. Now, a class-action lawsuit and investigations have started flying from almost everywhere.This development is not unexpected, as basic securities law allows shareholders to sue their investees if they misrepresent facts or otherwise perform actions that cause a drop in stock prices. They may have a point, as Nvidia's shares dipped significantly when the confirmation of Jensen's infidelity and the ramifications thereof hit the press everywhere.The legal proceedings are bound to be numerous, but as of right now, the first class-action lawsuit was filed by the Rosen Law Firm. The suit claims that Nvidia and Jensen Huang failed to disclose or misled investors regarding Jensen's affair with Alice, lied about it when asked, raised national security concerns, and caused a subsequent loss of Nvidia's reputation. You can check out the case docket at PacerMonitor here.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While legal analysis is beyond the scope of this news, Nvidia did downplay Jensen's relationship with Alice, saying that "Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year."Other legal firms have launched their own investigations into the recent development, with essentially the same justification: Schall, Brown & Schwartz attributes a 5.5% pre-market-trading drop to Nvidia, as does Levi & Korsinsky. The office of Frank R. Cruz mentions an 8.8% figure related to intra-day exchanging, and is interested in shareholders with $50,000 in losses. The percentage-drop figure is 5.88% premarket for Bronstein, Gewritz & Grossman. You may like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to having an affair with suspected Chinese spy US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to Congress over affair with alleged Chinese spy Every investigation and suit mentioned here requires no upfront fees from complainants, as with most class-action lawsuits. The underlying condition is often that the law firms involved get a cut of whichever damages or settlements may appear at the end of the lawsuit. history.titleZh: 律所对英伟达提起集体诉讼，此前CEO黄仁勋承认与一名被指为中国间谍的女子有婚外情
history.descriptionZh:
英伟达CEO黄仁勋近日承认与Alice Huang（与黄仁勋家族无亲属关系）存在婚外情。美国情报机构称，Alice Huang是中国“蜜罐”特工，任务包括协助将英伟达先进GPU走私到中国。这一确认引发英伟达股价显著下跌，并招致股东集体诉讼和多起调查。

背景上，美国对华实施先进GPU出口管制，英伟达相关产品受严格限制。情报界所称的“蜜罐”行动通常利用个人关系获取信息或便利非法交易，本案中据称涉及GPU走私。根据美国证券法，若公司或高管对重大事实作虚假陈述，或采取导致股价下跌的行动，股东可提起诉讼。因此，黄仁勋承认婚外情及其国家安全影响曝光后，英伟达股价下挫，诉讼随之而来。该新闻主要聚焦法律与声誉影响，未展开GPU具体技术原理。

首起集体诉讼由Rosen Law Firm提起。诉状称，英伟达和黄仁勋未披露或误导投资者关于黄与Alice关系的信息，在被问询时撒谎，引发国家安全担忧，并导致英伟达声誉受损。其他律所也启动调查，理由类似：Schall, Brown & Schwartz和Levi & Korsinsky均引用英伟达盘前交易下跌5.5%的数据；Frank R. Cruz提及日内交易中8.8%的跌幅，并寻求损失达5万美元的股东；Bronstein, Gewritz & Grossman则引用5.88%的盘前跌幅。这些集体诉讼通常不要求原告预付费用，律所从最终赔偿或和解中分成。Levi & Korsinsky还表示，即使投资者已亏损卖出英伟达股票也可参与，且无最低损失金额要求。

英伟达试图淡化黄仁勋与Alice的关系，称“Megaspeed与许多其他地区云客户并无不同。与客户会面是CEO工作的一部分；黄仁勋每年与数千名客户高管交流。”但法律程序预计将大量涌现。此事件不仅涉及个人道德问题，更牵涉国家安全、出口管制和公司治理，可能对英伟达的声誉和股价造成持续影响。
